Weekly Family Update - 09.10.26 
Headteacher’s Update: Keeping You Informed About What Matters 
Most 
Thank you for your continued support in helping your child attend school every day. Regular 
attendance is one of the most important factors in a young person's success, wellbeing and 
sense of belonging at school. 
Every lesson matters. Being in school each day helps students build strong relationships, 
develop confidence, keep up with learning and make the most of the opportunities available 
to them. Even missing occasional days can make it harder for students to stay connected to 
their learning. 
As we approach the half-term break, we would be grateful for your support in ensuring 
students attend every day until the end of term. Students finish for half term on Thursday 22 
October. 
Please note that the following are Meridian Trust INSET days, when students are not in 
school: 
• Friday 23 October 
• Monday 2 November 
This means students will have an extended break before returning to school on Tuesday 3 
November, giving plenty of time to rest and recharge. 
Thank you for working with us to ensure students are in school, on time, every day. Your 
support makes a real difference. 
Every day in school is a day of learning, friendship and opportunity. 
Andy Christoforou, Headteacher 

 
Please read on for essential updates. 
Vacancies at Abbey College and across the Meridian Trust 
https://www.abbey.college/vacancies  
Celebration of Spirit - Recognition 
 

Headteacher Commendations w/c 05/10/26 
The following students have been awarded with Headteacher's Commendations this week 
for going above and beyond in an area of school life.  They will receive 10 Spirit points and a 
special postcard home. 

 

 
Staff member of the week 
Miss Andrew-Martin: Passion - Your love for creative writing is infectious. To have 30 
students regularly attending an OOP and being so proud of the work they produce there is 
wonderful to see. Thank you for being so willing to give up your time to allow students to 
feel such a sense of pride and belonging. 
Tell us about something brilliant! 

If you would like to nominate someone for an Abbey College Spirit Award for any out of 
school success stories, then please follow this link or email the Office office@abbey.college . 
Strong Partnerships 
Parent's Forum 
Parent's Forum Update 
At last night’s Parent's Forum meeting, Mrs Noble provided an overview of the changes to 
the Relationships and Sex Education (RSE) guidance and invited feedback from parents. If 
you would like to contribute, please submit any comments here:  
• Relationships, Sex and Health Education: Parent Consultation – Fill in form.  
We look forward to using your feedback to help shape our updated policy, which will be 
published next year. 
We also continued planning for our exciting fundraising quiz on 12th November, and 
preparations are well underway. 
At our next Parent's Forum meeting, Miss Lane will provide an update on how our new Year 
7 students are settling into life at Abbey College and we will look at some projects to donate 
funds to. 
• Please email ParentsForum@abbey.college any questions.  
• Please find our minutes here: https://www.abbey.college/parents-forum  
• If you would like further information on the Parent's Forum, please email: 
ParentsForum@abbey.college   
Genevieve Wardle - Chair of Parent's Forum 
Family Quiz Night! 
The Abbey College Parents' Forum invites families to a fun-filled Family Quiz Night on 
Thursday 12th November in the South Hall. 
Gather a team of up to six people for £6 per team, test your knowledge, and compete for 
prizes, all while supporting a great cause.  
There are prizes which have been donated for a raffle on the night.    

The sixth form will be running the quiz so any support would be much appreciated! 
Every penny raised will go towards exciting new opportunities and resources for Abbey 
College students. 
 
Up-to-date MCAS details 
Please ensure that your contact details are kept up to date on MCAS (MyChildAtSchool). 
Having the correct information helps us contact you quickly if needed and ensures you 
receive important school communications. 

You can update your details yourself at any time through the MCAS app or website. 
Alternatively, if you need assistance, please email office@abbey.college with your updated 
information. 
Road Safety 
 
Zebra Crossing location Survey 
The County Council would like feedback on a proposed Zebra Crossing location near the 
school. Please complete the survey here: https://yourvoice.cambridgeshire.gov.uk/place-
and-sustainability/ramsey-zebra-crossing-feedback/ 
Any queries, please contact Hanane Rouadi, Assistant Project Manager, Local Improvements 
Team, Hanane.Rouadi@cambridgeshire.gov.uk 
Diary Dates  
 
��� Inset Days Coming Up 
Please note that the following are Meridian Trust-wide Inset Days. All Meridian Trust 
schools, including Abbey College, will be closed to students on these dates: 
������������ Friday 23 October 
������������Monday 2 November 

������������Friday 27 November 
���� Please add these dates to your family calendar. 
These training days allow staff from across Meridian Trust to work together, share best 
practice and continue to improve the education we provide for all students. 
Everything You Need to Know About Assessments 
 
Ensuring Pupils Feel Safe and Behave Well 
Safety First 
Healthy Habits 
This week students discussed healthy habits, hygiene, hydration, sleep and self-care. 
We encouraged students to consider how everyday health habits support both wellbeing 
and school attendance. 
Useful Resources 
• NHS Live Well: https://www.nhs.uk/live-well 
• NHS Better Health: https://www.nhs.uk/better-health 
• The Sleep Charity: https://thesleepcharity.org.uk 
If you need support or have any concerns about your child's wellbeing or safety, please 
contact welfare@abbey.college 
Promoting Positive Behaviour Every Day 
Student attendance  
Week 5 – Coughs & Colds  

It’s okay to feel under the weather sometimes—but most coughs and colds don’t need days 
off school.  
If you’re well enough, being in school helps you stay on track.  
Don’t let a small illness lead to big gaps in learning.  
Ms Davis – Attendance Officer 
Supporting Your Child’s Wider Development 
Offer & Opportunity Programme (OOPs) - Autumn Term 
 

 
 
 
Click here 
Student curriculum 
How can I find out what my child is learning in each subject? 
Learning outside the classroom (LoTC) 
At Abbey College, we believe learning should extend beyond the classroom. Through a wide 
range of opportunities, students can experience art, culture, heritage, adventure and the 
natural world, helping to broaden their horizons and build confidence. These enriching 
experiences are offered through our curriculum and our Offer and Opportunity Programme 
(OOP), alongside trips, visits and activities such as the Combined Cadet Force (CCF). The aim 
is to give every student access to memorable experiences that support their personal growth 
and development.  
Find out more: Learning Outside the Classroom 
Communicating with us and raising concerns 
Click here to access this Communication Flowchart on our website. 

Parent Friendly Policy Guide: 
https://www.abbey.college/key-policies--reports  
Other news updates can be found here: 
• Our news page: https://www.abbey.college/school-communications  
• Facebook: https://www.facebook.com/pg/RamseyAbbeyCollege/posts/  
• Instagram: https://www.instagram.com/abbeycollege_ramsey/

Weekly Family Update - 16.10.26 
Headteacher’s Update: Keeping You Informed About What 
Matters Most 
Our virtue this week was Passion - going above and beyond what is expected. Our focus was: 
"We show focus and use positive language." Students explored the importance of speaking 
respectfully to adults and one another, using polite language and good manners, including 
phrases such as "excuse me", "please" and "thank you". 
Our Welfare Wednesday message focused on staying safe when travelling to and from 
school. Students were reminded to stay alert, particularly when crossing roads, and to avoid 
distractions such as headphones and mobile phones. We also spoke to cyclists about the 
importance of wearing a helmet and ensuring their bicycle is safe and roadworthy. 
This message is especially important at the moment as our building project continues to 
make excellent progress. While the work is carefully managed, we continue to remind 
students to stay aware of their surroundings, follow designated routes and make sensible 
choices around the site. The same focus, awareness and responsibility that keeps students 
safe on their journey to school is equally important during the school day. 
There will be no Weekly Update next week. Instead, we will be sharing our Half-Term 
Community Round-Up, celebrating the many achievements, events and successes from 
across the school this half term. 
Have a lovely weekend. 
Andy Christoforou, Headteacher 
Road Closure: 24 October until 6 November 2026 
We have been given notice that Upwood Road, Bury will be closed, which may affect 
parents, guardians, and staff travelling to and from the school. There will be diversions in 
place, but you will need to allow extra travel time. 

 
Please read on for essential updates. 
Vacancies at Abbey College and across the Meridian Trust 
https://www.abbey.college/vacancies  
Celebration of Spirit - Recognition 
Non-Uniform days for Spirit Ratio 
Congratulations to all our Year groups for meeting their new spirit ratios 
this half term.  Each year group will be rewarded with a non-uniform 
day.  Please ensure your child wears clothing that is appropriate for 
school. 
 
Headteacher Commendations w/c 12/10/26 
The following students have been awarded with Headteacher's Commendations this week 
for going above and beyond in an area of school life.  They will receive 10 Spirit points and a 
special postcard home. 

 
 

Staff member of the week 
Mr Kidze - Intuition: Students were highly engaged throughout the lesson. Regular retrieval 
activities helped them recall and strengthen their learning, while thoughtful questioning 
encouraged everyone to take part and contribute confidently. 
Tell us about something brilliant! 
If you would like to nominate someone for an Abbey College Spirit Award for any out of 
school success stories, then please follow this 
link or email the Office office@abbey.college . 
Strong Partnerships 
Parent's Forum 
Parent's Forum Update 
At last night’s Parent's Forum meeting, Mrs Noble provided an 
overview of the changes to the Relationships and Sex Education (RSE) guidance and invited 
feedback from parents. If you would like to contribute, please submit any comments here:  
• Relationships, Sex and Health Education: Parent Consultation – Fill in form.  
We look forward to using your feedback to help shape our updated policy, which will be 
published next year. 
We also continued planning for our exciting fundraising quiz on 12th November, and 
preparations are well underway. 
At our next Parent's Forum meeting, Miss Lane will provide an update on how our new Year 
7 students are settling into life at Abbey College and we will look at some projects to donate 
funds to. 
• Please email ParentsForum@abbey.college any questions.  
• Please find our minutes here: https://www.abbey.college/parents-forum  
• If you would like further information on the Parent's Forum, please email: 
ParentsForum@abbey.college   
Genevieve Wardle - Chair of Parent's Forum 
Family Quiz Night! 
The Abbey College Parents' Forum invites families to a fun-filled Family Quiz Night on 
Thursday 12th November in the South Hall. 

Gather a team of up to six people for £6 per team, test your knowledge, and compete for 
prizes, all while supporting a great cause.  
There are prizes which have been donated for a raffle on the night.    
The sixth form will be running the quiz so any support would be much appreciated! 
Every penny raised will go towards exciting new opportunities and resources for Abbey 
College students. 
 
Up-to-date MCAS details 

Please ensure that your contact details are kept up to date on MCAS (MyChildAtSchool). 
Having the correct information helps us contact you quickly if needed and ensures you 
receive important school communications. 
You can update your details yourself at any time through the MCAS app or website. 
Alternatively, if you need assistance, please email office@abbey.college with your updated 
information. 
Diary Dates  
 
    Inset Days Coming Up 
Please note that the following are Meridian Trust-wide Inset Days. All Meridian Trust 
schools, including Abbey College, will be closed to students on these dates: 
             Friday 23 October 
            Monday 2 November 
            Friday 27 November 
     Please add these dates to your family calendar. 
These training days allow staff from across Meridian Trust to work together, share best 
practice and continue to improve the education we provide for all students. 
Everything You Need to Know About Assessments 
 

Ensuring Pupils Feel Safe and Behave Well 
Safety First 
Road Safety 
Students were reminded this week about safe travel, including road safety, cycling safety, bus 
behaviour and remaining aware of their surroundings. 
The importance of respectful behaviour on school transport and safe travel was reinforced. 
Useful Resources 
• THINK!: https://www.think.gov.uk 
• Bikeability: https://www.bikeability.org.uk 
• Brake: https://www.brake.org.uk 
• Child Accident Prevention Trust: https://capt.org.uk 
If you need support or have any concerns about your child's wellbeing or safety, please 
contact welfare@abbey.college 
Police Liaison Officer Visits to School 
We are pleased to welcome Hannah Watkins, our School Liaison Officer, who visits school 
regularly. Hannah works closely with local secondary schools and provides valuable support 
to students, families and staff. 
Having a visible police presence in school helps students build positive relationships with 
local police officers, promotes trust and confidence, and provides an additional source of 
support and advice for young people. Hannah can also support the school with safeguarding 
concerns, advice around community issues affecting young people, and welfare checks 
where appropriate. 
We believe these visits are a positive addition to our school community and help strengthen 
links between school, families and local services, ensuring that our students feel safe, 
supported and well-informed. If you do have any questions or concerns regarding these 
visits please get in touch with the welfare team: welfare@abbey.college 
Promoting Positive Behaviour Every Day 
Neutral Behaviour Events 
We have added ‘neutral’ behaviour events to MCAS to help keep you informed. 
Please do not worry. These are not sanctions. It is simply a way for us to keep you informed 
when your child has received some extra support linked to their behaviour or attendance.  
If you have questions about these, please contact your child's form tutor. 

Student attendance  
Week 6 – Persistent Absence (PA) & Life Chances  
Missing just a few days each term soon adds up and can seriously impact your future.  
Students with lower attendance are more likely to struggle with exams and next steps.  
Aim high, 6 days or lesson off per year gives you the best chance of success.  
Ms Davis – Attendance Officer 
Supporting Your Child’s Wider Development 
Offer & Opportunity Programme (OOPs) - Autumn Term  
 
 

 
Click here 
School Trips 
The school trips calendar can be found on the website: https://www.abbey.college/learning-
outside-the-classroom  
 
Student curriculum 
How can I find out what my child is learning in each subject? 
Wider Personal Development 
At present, we are conducting our annual consultation on the Relationships, Sex and Health 
Education Policy. To read how this fits in with our Wider Personal Development Programme, 
click the link below. 
Find out more: https://www.abbey.college/wider-personal-development  
 
Communicating with us and raising concerns 
Click here to access this Communication Flowchart on our website. 
Parent Friendly Policy Guide: 
https://www.abbey.college/key-policies--reports  
Other news updates can be found here: 
• Our news page: https://www.abbey.college/school-communications  
• Facebook: https://www.facebook.com/pg/RamseyAbbeyCollege/posts/  
• Instagram: https://www.instagram.com/abbeycollege_ramsey/

Matters Most 
It has been lovely to welcome students back after the half-term break, and we have had a positive start 
to the new half term. 
We started the new half term by focusing on the virtue of Humility: “We accept praise, recognise others 
and apologise immediately.” 
Mrs Noble also led our Reset Assemblies, giving students time to celebrate what went well last half term 
and think about what they can do even better. We were delighted that every year group achieved our 
minimum 12:1 Spirit Ratio, earning their non-uniform rewards. Our aim is for every year group to achieve 
this again this half term. 
For Welfare Wednesday, students explored anti-social behaviour and the impact our actions can have on 
others. With darker evenings and events such as firework displays taking place, we asked students to 
show maturity and emotional intelligence when out in the community. How we behave matters, and we 
want our students to help others feel safe and respected. 
Andy Christoforou, Headteacher

Headteacher’s Update: Keeping You Informed About What Matters Most 
Remembrance Day: A Moment of Unity 
Remembrance has been marked with great care across our school this week.  
On Wednesday 11 November, our whole school came together to observe a two-minute silence for 
Armistice Day. Students who are members of the CCF, other local cadet forces and Scouts also wore 
their uniforms, adding a special connection to the occasion. Mr Patterson delivered a powerful 
speech, followed by readings from our Year 8 pupils, who had written their own poems. A selection of 
these is shared below. 
Remembrance gives us time to pause, reflect and come together. The respect shown by our students 
and staff is always moving and reflects the values we share as a school community. 
Every Day at School Matters 
Term 2 is short, with an INSET day on Friday 27 November. We expect all students to attend every 
school day through to the end of term on Friday 18 December. 
You can check our full term dates here. Please check these dates before making plans and do not 
book holidays during term time. 
Every day at school matters.

news.content: Weekly Family Update - 13.11.26 Headteacher’s Update: Keeping You Informed About What Matters Most Remembrance Day: A Moment of Unity Remembrance has been marked with great care across our school this week. On Wednesday 11 November, our whole school came together to observe a two-minute silence for Armistice Day. Students who are members of the CCF, other local cadet forces and Scouts also wore their uniforms, adding a special connection to the occasion. Mr Patterson delivered a powerful speech, followed by readings from our Year 8 pupils, who had written their own poems. A selection of these is shared below. Remembrance gives us time to pause, reflect and come together. The respect shown by our students and staff is always moving and reflects the values we share as a school community. Eve

201. County and District Councillor Update: 
Apologies were received from Cllr J Sidlow County Councillor. Cllr S Corney informed the members as the election is now 
on there would not be many meetings being held. Cllr J Clarke informed the members that he had attended Licensing but 
none of the items affected Ramsey Parish directly.

1.1 26/00623/FUL Change of use of land to a gypsy and traveller residential site comprising the siting of two

seconded by Cllr M Clarke Ramsey Town Council voted UNANIMOUSLY to ask the District Council to REFUSE 
the application. Members feedback was the site does not have the appropriate amenities in place, the distance 
sited to reach the local school and doctors was incorrect and much further. The area is close to a site of natural

movement. Council noted there were no recorded neighbouring objections but had received communication 
directly to the office and the Mayor objecting to the application.

RAMSEY TOWN COUNCIL 
 
You are hereby summoned to attend a meeting of Ramsey Town Council to be held in The Lavender Room, 
Ramsey Town Council Great Whyte, Ramsey on Thursday 28th May 2026 at 7.00pm, when the following 
items of business will be transacted: - 
 
 
Please ensure all mobile phones are switched off or turned to silent during the meeting.

 Lisa Renfree                           22nd May 2026

MINUTES OF RAMSEY TOWN COUNCIL MEETING 
held at 7pm on Thursday 14 May 2026 (AGM) at  
Ramsey Town Council Great Whyte, Ramsey 
 
 
Present:  Councillors: J Aubin, A Austin, I Axelsen, J Bufton, M Clarke, J Clarke, S Corney (Dep Mayor), A Costello, S 
Fice, V Fendley (Mayor), L Knight, C Maskell, P Rose, and E Welsh. 
In attendance: Mrs Lisa Renfree, Town Clerk  
 
Cllr V Fendley welcomed all the Councillors back who had been elected uncontested and welcomed new Councillor Ian 
Axelsen. 
 
Cllr V Fendley chaired this section of the meeting until the proposal was made and Cllr S Corney took the vote. 
216. Election of Town Mayor for 2026/27 – Cllr S Corney proposed Cllr V Fendley. Cllr S Corney stated that he felt Cllr V 
Fendley deserved to stay to see the fruition of the Ramsey Neighbourhood Community Plan and other local projects. Cllr A 
Austin seconded the proposal. No other nominations were made. Ramsey Town Council members voted UNANIMOUSLY 
for Cllr V Fendley to be Ramsey Town Council Mayor for 2026/27. Cllr V Fendley graciously accepted and stated that she 
was humbled to be voted in again and that it had been a privilege to serve for the previous two years. Cllr V Fendley did 
state that this would be her last year in the civic role. 
 
217. Election of Deputy Town Mayor for 2026/27 – Cllr V Fendley proposed Cllr S Corney for the position, Cllr V Fendley 
stated that she felt Cllr S Corney brought stability to the role but would encourage other councillors to support both herself 
and the Deputy to gain experience in understanding the role for future years. This proposal was seconded by Cllr J Bufton. 
Cllr V Fendley then asked if there were any other nominations for the position of Deputy. Cllr L Knight stated that she 
would be interested in the position, but no nomination was made. Ramsey Town Council members voted UNANIMOUSLY 
for Cllr S Corney to be the Deputy Mayor for 2026/27. Cllr S Corney reiterated that he would welcome other Councillors 
joining him at events to learn the position for the future. 
 
218. Apologies for Absence: Cllrs R Cope, and R Terrill. 
 
219.To  Receive  Declarations  of  Interest: There  were  no  declarations  at  this  point  in  the  meeting,  but  Cllr  L  Knight 
declared  a  non-pecuniary  interest  in  minute  no.226  as  the  treasurer  of  Ramsey  Memory  Support  Group.  Cllr  V  Fendley 
declared an interest in minute number 230 as a committee member of Creative Crafters. Cllrs J Aubin & I Axelsen declared 
a non-pecuniary interest in 229 (f) as Trustees of Ramsey Neighbourhoods Trust. 
 
220. Public  Participation: There  were  8  members  of  the  public  present.  Cllr  R  Coogan  and  Cllr  K  Maheshwari  newly 
elected  District  Councillors  addressed  members,  both  were  invited  to  make  an  appointment  with  the  Clerk  and  find  out 
more about Ramsey Town Council projects. Cllr H Tobias newly elected District Councillor sent his apologies. Cllr J Sidlow 
County Councillor sent his apologies and asked the Clerk to circulate his report.    
 
221.  Minutes  of  the  Last  Meeting  to  be  Approved: Proposed  by  Cllr  S  Fice  and  Seconded  by  Cllr  S  Corney,  Council 
voted UNANIMOUSLY to APPROVE the Minutes of the meeting of 23rd April 2026 as a correct record. 
 
222. Planning Applications for Consideration 
1.1 26/00681/FUL Construction of 2 no. drive-thru units (sui generis) with associated hard and soft landscaping – Plot 9A St 
Marys Road, Ramsey. Proposed by Cllr S Corney and seconded by Cllr P Rose, Ramsey Town Council voted 
UNANIMOUSLY for the District Council to APPROVE the application. Members noted the Highways comments and wanted 
to ensure there would be a pathway built at the time of development and not require further funding in the future. 
 
1.2 26/00756/HHFUL Proposed erection of porch, pitched roof to existing garage, external alterations to existing rear 
extension and garage and internal alterations – The Lavenders, 38 Biggin Lane, Ramsey. Proposed by Cllr P Rose and 
seconded by Cllr S Fice, Ramsey Town Council voted UNANIMOUSLY for the District Council to APPROVE the 
application. Council noted there were no neighbouring objections. 
 
1.3 26/00085/FUL Conversion of two dwellings into one dwelling with replacement front porch 135-137 Great Whyte, 
Ramsey. Proposed by Cllr S Corney and seconded by Cllr P Rose, Ramsey Town Council voted UNANIMOUSLY for the 
District Council to APPROVE the application. Council noted that there were no neighbouring objections. 
 
223. THE PARISH COUNCILS (GENERAL POWER OF COMPETENCE) (PRESCRIBED CONDITIONS) Order 2012. 
To resolve to agree that the Council meets the conditions of eligibility required to exercise the General Power of 
Competence as set out in the Parish Councils (General Power of Competence) (Prescribed Conditions) Order 2012 with 
immediate effect. - Report previously circulated. Ramsey Town council now meets the criteria for having General Power 
of Competence as the Clerk had the CiLCA qualification and a minimum of twelve of their Councillors had been elected. 
Proposed by Cllr S Corney and seconded by Cllr E Welsh, Ramsey Town Council voted UNANIMOUSLY to resolve to 
agree that the Council meets the conditions of eligibility required to exercise the General Power of Competence as set 
out in the Parish Councils (General Power of Competence) (Prescribed Conditions) Order 2012 with immediate effect.  
 

224. REVIEW OF THE COUNCIL’S POLICIES, PROCEDURES, REGULATIONS AND DELEGATED POWERS. 
Councillors are requested to follow the link (control and click) to the Town Council’s policies prior to the meeting in order 
to suggest any amendments required. Proposed by Cllr C Maskell and seconded by Cllr J Aubin Ramsey Town Council 
voted 13 FOR and 1 ABSTENTION to APPROVE the online policies. It was noted that throughout the financial year 
2026/7 working parties can recommend any changes and bring to Full Council for approval. 
 
225. FINANCIAL MATTERS:  
 a) Financial Summary – Cash Book to 30/4/26 – The Clerk was asked about the funds left as reserves in the bank not 
yet allocated, the Clerk explained that the funds are allocated to working parties but not to actual projects. The new finance 
system will allow Chairs of the working parties to look into their allocated budget, the Clerk informed members this was in 
the final stages of being set up. Council noted the cash book. 
 b) Expenditure transactions to be tabled and approved. Proposed by Cllr L Knight and    seconded by Cllr S Fice 
Ramsey Town Council voted UNANIMOUSLY for the expenditure transactions to be APPROVED. 
      Cllr L Knight asked the Clerk why the meeting of the chairman of the working parties had not been organised. The 
Mayor explained the new working parties would be agreed that night and then the chairmen of those working parties 
would set up their own meetings. 
 
 226. WORKING PARTY RECOMMENDATIONS 
 Employment Working Party – To recommend Council agree the Service Level Agreement between Ramsey Town 
Council and Ramsey Memory Support Group. Cllr L Knight declared a non-pecuniary interest as treasurer of the 
Ramsey Memory Support Group. Proposed by Cllr A Costello and seconded by Cllr A Austin, the Service Level 
Agreement between Ramsey Town Council and Ramsey Support Group was APPROVED by 12 FOR and 2 
ABSTENTIONS. The Mayor signed the document. 
 
227. NEW WORKING PARTIES 
 To decide on appointments to the new working parties: 
• Economic Development 
• Highways and Infrastructure 
• Amenities Health and Leisure 
• Finance and Office 
• Communications 
• Strategic 
• Cemetery 
The new titled Working Parties had now come into effect. Each Councillor agreed which working party they wanted to sit on. 
The Clerk to circulate the completed list once Cllrs Cope and Terrill sent their preferences. 
 
228. TOWN COUNCIL REPRESENTATIVES ON EXTERNAL ORGANISATIONS.   
 To appoint town council representatives on external organisations -  
Bury & Traffic Liaison            Cllr V Fendley 
Cambridgeshire Policing Liaison   Cllr Terrill 
Health & Safety Officer           Cllr P Rose 
Hunts Volunteer Centre (Ramsey)  Cllr J Aubin 
Middle Level Navigation Advisory Cttee  Cllr S Corney 
Parish Forum    Cllr V Fendley 
Pavilion Management Committee    Cllr C Maskell/ Cllr A Costello 
Heritage Partnership   Cllr C Maskell 
Ramsey Welfare Charity   Cllr P Rose/ Cllr M Clarke/ Pat Taylor/ Alan 
Johnson 
Red Tile Wind Farm Trust  Cllr A Costello 
Spinning Trust  Cllr E Welsh 
Youth Services Liaison  Cllr C Maskell 
Hunts Visitor Economy Partnership Cllr C Maskell 
 
229. TOWN MAYOR’S AND CLERK’S CORRESPONDENCE: 
 a) Update on town improvements – The Clerk updated council that the TRO is still delayed and potentially work may 
start in September. Noted 
 b) Update on skatepark path and moorings – members were informed that the Skate park path was now installed. A 
discussion took place about the communication to the residents about the work taking place. It was agreed around the table 
it had not been good enough and Cllr L Knight asked for it to be minuted and that it should be discussed at the 
Communication Working Party on 19
th
 May. The Moorings work will be completed by 23
rd
 May, the delay had been sourcing 
the brickwork. 
      c) New employee- Quincy Bastow – the Clerk informed the members that the new Admin Assistant had started work and 
finished the four-day induction. 
 d) Civic Service – 20th September 2026 Noted 

 e) District Councillor update – the Mayor updated the members on the newly elected District Councillors and in the 
public participation they had spoken. There will be a designated agenda item moving forward to keep Ramsey Town Council 
informed of their work in the community. 
f) To agree to a request by Ramsey Neighbourhoods Trust to host the Youth Connection Bus on QE2 Park in July and 
August. – After a long discussion it was agreed that the bus should be parked on the road with the doors facing the 
park. Ramsey Town Council did not want the bus on the grassed area. 
g) Feedback from work experience. The Clerk informed Council that over the previous month they had had 8 Abbey 
College year 10 for work experience, 1 Abbey College sixth form student and four sixth form students from 
Hinchingbrooke school sixth form. noted 
h) Ramsey Communities Neighbourhood Plan Update. Cllr V Fendley updated members that the Ramsey Communities 
Neighbourhood plan had moved to the next formal stage which is led by Huntingdonshire District Council, and they will 
then appoint an Independent Assessor. It is very rare for there not to be any required amendments but there were not 
any on our plan. Noted  
 i)  To agree to Creative Crafters using the Market Charter to hold a Makers and Bakers Market on Sunday 28
th
 June, 
26
th
 July and 30
th
 August 2026, road closure 8am-5pm event 10-3pm. After a long discussion proposed by Cllr A Austin 
and seconded by Cllr E Welsh Ramsey Town Council voted 13 FOR and 1 ABSTENTION for the Creative Crafters to 
use the Market charter but it would be reviewed after each event. 
 
230. ATTENDANCES AT MEETINGS OR ORGANISATIONS: 
• VE Memorial – The Clerk informed members that Cllr R Terrill attended the event and laid a 
wreath on behalf of Ramsey Town Council. 
• Biodiversity Fun Day- The Clerk informed members that the day was successful and 
approximately sixty children had attended.  
• Cllr S Corney informed members he had attended the Bio-diversity day. Cllr L Knight asked that it 
be minuted to thank the PCC for the use of electricity for the bouncy castle and the cakes and 
drink supplied for the event. 
• Cllr V Fendley attended the Ramsey Abbey Road Safety meeting where it was discussed that 
they are separating the two projects as further discussion was required on the zebra crossing but 
they wanted the road cushions to go ahead. 
• Cllr V Fendley informed members the quote had been received for a Planning Consultant – this 
was to be sent to the Finance and Office Working Party. 
• Cllr A Austin informed members he had attended the CEO breakfast at Huntingdonshire District 
Council. 
• Cllr A Austin informed members he had attended the Youth Safe Space at St Thomas a Becket 
Church, he stated they had 170 children through the doors and 28 of them stayed for the whole 
hour, Cllr A Austin encouraged members to volunteer if they could. A discussion took place for the 
Clerk to look into DBS checks for members going to events such as this. 
• Cllr L Knight informed members that she had attended the Melodies in May concert at St Thomas 
a Becket Church on behalf of the Council and Mr Richard Hyde MBE asked her to say some 
closing remarks where Cllr L Knight promoted Bands on the Green. 
• Cllr V Fendley attended the U3A 15
th
 Anniversary event and informed members they had 236 
members and 32 interest groups. 
• Cllr V Fendley informed members she had attended the St George’s Day Service in Huntingdon. 
• Cllr V Fendley informed Council that she represented Ramsey Town Council in place of Cllr C 
Maskell at the Local Visitor Economy Partnership and their next meeting on 14
th
 July will be in 
Ramsey. 
Cllr M Clarke asked for a minuted vote of thanks to the outgoing District Councillors, Cllr A Costello, Cllr J Clarke and Cllr S 
Corney for their dedication and hard work over many years. The Councillors had a round of applause. 
 
231. Meeting Dates 
The next meeting of Ramsey Town Council (Planning) will take place on 28
th
 May 2026 at 7pm.

Present:  Councillors: J Aubin, A Austin, I Axelsen, J Bufton, M Clarke, J Clarke, S Corney (Dep Mayor), A Costello, S Fice, V Fendley (Mayor), L Knight, C Maskell, P Rose, and E Welsh. In attendance: Mrs Lisa Renfree, Town Clerk
Cllr V Fendley welcomed all the Councillors back who had been elected uncontested and welcomed new Councillor Ian Axelsen.

Cllr V Fendley chaired this section of the meeting until the proposal was made and Cllr S Corney took the vote. 216. Election of Town Mayor for 2026/27 – Cllr S Corney proposed Cllr V Fendley. Cllr S Corney stated that he felt Cllr V Fendley deserved to stay to see the fruition of the Ramsey Neighbourhood Community Plan and other local projects. Cllr A Austin seconded the proposal. No other nominations were made. Ramsey Town Council members voted UNANIMOUSLY for Cllr V Fendley to be Ramsey Town Council Mayor for 2026/27. Cllr V Fendley graciously accepted and stated that she was humbled to be voted in again and that it had been a privilege to serve for the previous two years. Cllr V Fendley did state that this would be her last year in the civic role.

217. Election of Deputy Town Mayor for 2026/27 – Cllr V Fendley proposed Cllr S Corney for the position, Cllr V Fendley stated that she felt Cllr S Corney brought stability to the role but would encourage other councillors to support both herself and the Deputy to gain experience in understanding the role for future years. This proposal was seconded by Cllr J Bufton. Cllr V Fendley then asked if there were any other nominations for the position of Deputy. Cllr L Knight stated that she would be interested in the position, but no nomination was made. Ramsey Town Council members voted UNANIMOUSLY for Cllr S Corney to be the Deputy Mayor for 2026/27. Cllr S Corney reiterated that he would welcome other Councillors joining him at events to learn the position for the future.
218. Apologies for Absence: Cllrs R Cope, and R Terrill.

219.To  Receive  Declarations  of  Interest: There  were  no  declarations  at  this  point  in  the  meeting,  but  Cllr  L  Knight declared  a  non-pecuniary  interest  in  minute  no.226  as  the  treasurer  of  Ramsey  Memory  Support  Group.  Cllr  V  Fendley declared an interest in minute number 230 as a committee member of Creative Crafters. Cllrs J Aubin & I Axelsen declared a non-pecuniary interest in 229 (f) as Trustees of Ramsey Neighbourhoods Trust.

220. Public  Participation: There  were  8  members  of  the  public  present.  Cllr  R  Coogan  and  Cllr  K  Maheshwari  newly elected  District  Councillors  addressed  members,  both  were  invited  to  make  an  appointment  with  the  Clerk  and  find  out more about Ramsey Town Council projects. Cllr H Tobias newly elected District Councillor sent his apologies. Cllr J Sidlow County Councillor sent his apologies and asked the Clerk to circulate his report.

221.  Minutes  of  the  Last  Meeting  to  be  Approved: Proposed  by  Cllr  S  Fice  and  Seconded  by  Cllr  S  Corney,  Council voted UNANIMOUSLY to APPROVE the Minutes of the meeting of 23rd April 2026 as a correct record.

222. Planning Applications for Consideration 1.1 26/00681/FUL Construction of 2 no. drive-thru units (sui generis) with associated hard and soft landscaping – Plot 9A St Marys Road, Ramsey. Proposed by Cllr S Corney and seconded by Cllr P Rose, Ramsey Town Council voted UNANIMOUSLY for the District Council to APPROVE the application. Members noted the Highways comments and wanted to ensure there would be a pathway built at the time of development and not require further funding in the future.

1.2 26/00756/HHFUL Proposed erection of porch, pitched roof to existing garage, external alterations to existing rear extension and garage and internal alterations – The Lavenders, 38 Biggin Lane, Ramsey. Proposed by Cllr P Rose and seconded by Cllr S Fice, Ramsey Town Council voted UNANIMOUSLY for the District Council to APPROVE the application. Council noted there were no neighbouring objections.

1.3 26/00085/FUL Conversion of two dwellings into one dwelling with replacement front porch 135-137 Great Whyte, Ramsey. Proposed by Cllr S Corney and seconded by Cllr P Rose, Ramsey Town Council voted UNANIMOUSLY for the District Council to APPROVE the application. Council noted that there were no neighbouring objections.

223. THE PARISH COUNCILS (GENERAL POWER OF COMPETENCE) (PRESCRIBED CONDITIONS) Order 2012. To resolve to agree that the Council meets the conditions of eligibility required to exercise the General Power of Competence as set out in the Parish Councils (General Power of Competence) (Prescribed Conditions) Order 2012 with immediate effect. - Report previously circulated. Ramsey Town council now meets the criteria for having General Power of Competence as the Clerk had the CiLCA qualification and a minimum of twelve of their Councillors had been elected. Proposed by Cllr S Corney and seconded by Cllr E Welsh, Ramsey Town Council voted UNANIMOUSLY to resolve to agree that the Council meets the conditions of eligibility required to exercise the General Power of Competence as set out in the Parish Councils (General Power of Competence) (Prescribed Conditions) Order 2012 with immediate effect.

224. REVIEW OF THE COUNCIL’S POLICIES, PROCEDURES, REGULATIONS AND DELEGATED POWERS. Councillors are requested to follow the link (control and click) to the Town Council’s policies prior to the meeting in order to suggest any amendments required. Proposed by Cllr C Maskell and seconded by Cllr J Aubin Ramsey Town Council voted 13 FOR and 1 ABSTENTION to APPROVE the online policies. It was noted that throughout the financial year 2026/7 working parties can recommend any changes and bring to Full Council for approval.

225. FINANCIAL MATTERS: a) Financial Summary – Cash Book to 30/4/26 – The Clerk was asked about the funds left as reserves in the bank not yet allocated, the Clerk explained that the funds are allocated to working parties but not to actual projects. The new finance system will allow Chairs of the working parties to look into their allocated budget, the Clerk informed members this was in the final stages of being set up. Council noted the cash book. b) Expenditure transactions to be tabled and approved. Proposed by Cllr L Knight and    seconded by Cllr S Fice Ramsey Town Council voted UNANIMOUSLY for the expenditure transactions to be APPROVED. Cllr L Knight asked the Clerk why the meeting of the chairman of the working parties had not been organised. The Mayor explained the new working parties would be agreed that night and then the chairmen of those working parties would set up their own meetings.

226. WORKING PARTY RECOMMENDATIONS Employment Working Party – To recommend Council agree the Service Level Agreement between Ramsey Town Council and Ramsey Memory Support Group. Cllr L Knight declared a non-pecuniary interest as treasurer of the Ramsey Memory Support Group. Proposed by Cllr A Costello and seconded by Cllr A Austin, the Service Level Agreement between Ramsey Town Council and Ramsey Support Group was APPROVED by 12 FOR and 2 ABSTENTIONS. The Mayor signed the document.

227. NEW WORKING PARTIES To decide on appointments to the new working parties: • Economic Development • Highways and Infrastructure • Amenities Health and Leisure • Finance and Office • Communications • Strategic • Cemetery The new titled Working Parties had now come into effect. Each Councillor agreed which working party they wanted to sit on. The Clerk to circulate the completed list once Cllrs Cope and Terrill sent their preferences.

228. TOWN COUNCIL REPRESENTATIVES ON EXTERNAL ORGANISATIONS. To appoint town council representatives on external organisations - Bury & Traffic Liaison            Cllr V Fendley Cambridgeshire Policing Liaison   Cllr Terrill Health & Safety Officer           Cllr P Rose Hunts Volunteer Centre (Ramsey)  Cllr J Aubin Middle Level Navigation Advisory Cttee  Cllr S Corney Parish Forum    Cllr V Fendley Pavilion Management Committee    Cllr C Maskell/ Cllr A Costello Heritage Partnership   Cllr C Maskell Ramsey Welfare Charity   Cllr P Rose/ Cllr M Clarke/ Pat Taylor/ Alan Johnson Red Tile Wind Farm Trust  Cllr A Costello Spinning Trust  Cllr E Welsh Youth Services Liaison  Cllr C Maskell Hunts Visitor Economy Partnership Cllr C Maskell

229. TOWN MAYOR’S AND CLERK’S CORRESPONDENCE: a) Update on town improvements – The Clerk updated council that the TRO is still delayed and potentially work may start in September. Noted b) Update on skatepark path and moorings – members were informed that the Skate park path was now installed. A discussion took place about the communication to the residents about the work taking place. It was agreed around the table it had not been good enough and Cllr L Knight asked for it to be minuted and that it should be discussed at the Communication Working Party on 19 th May. The Moorings work will be completed by 23 rd May, the delay had been sourcing the brickwork. c) New employee- Quincy Bastow – the Clerk informed the members that the new Admin Assistant had started work and finished the four-day induction. d) Civic Service – 20th September 2026 Noted

e) District Councillor update – the Mayor updated the members on the newly elected District Councillors and in the public participation they had spoken. There will be a designated agenda item moving forward to keep Ramsey Town Council informed of their work in the community. f) To agree to a request by Ramsey Neighbourhoods Trust to host the Youth Connection Bus on QE2 Park in July and August. – After a long discussion it was agreed that the bus should be parked on the road with the doors facing the park. Ramsey Town Council did not want the bus on the grassed area. g) Feedback from work experience. The Clerk informed Council that over the previous month they had had 8 Abbey College year 10 for work experience, 1 Abbey College sixth form student and four sixth form students from Hinchingbrooke school sixth form. noted h) Ramsey Communities Neighbourhood Plan Update. Cllr V Fendley updated members that the Ramsey Communities Neighbourhood plan had moved to the next formal stage which is led by Huntingdonshire District Council, and they will then appoint an Independent Assessor. It is very rare for there not to be any required amendments but there were not any on our plan. Noted i)  To agree to Creative Crafters using the Market Charter to hold a Makers and Bakers Market on Sunday 28 th June, 26 th July and 30 th August 2026, road closure 8am-5pm event 10-3pm. After a long discussion proposed by Cllr A Austin and seconded by Cllr E Welsh Ramsey Town Council voted 13 FOR and 1 ABSTENTION for the Creative Crafters to use the Market charter but it would be reviewed after each event.

230. ATTENDANCES AT MEETINGS OR ORGANISATIONS: • VE Memorial – The Clerk informed members that Cllr R Terrill attended the event and laid a wreath on behalf of Ramsey Town Council. • Biodiversity Fun Day- The Clerk informed members that the day was successful and approximately sixty children had attended. • Cllr S Corney informed members he had attended the Bio-diversity day. Cllr L Knight asked that it be minuted to thank the PCC for the use of electricity for the bouncy castle and the cakes and drink supplied for the event. • Cllr V Fendley attended the Ramsey Abbey Road Safety meeting where it was discussed that they are separating the two projects as further discussion was required on the zebra crossing but they wanted the road cushions to go ahead. • Cllr V Fendley informed members the quote had been received for a Planning Consultant – this was to be sent to the Finance and Office Working Party. • Cllr A Austin informed members he had attended the CEO breakfast at Huntingdonshire District Council. • Cllr A Austin informed members he had attended the Youth Safe Space at St Thomas a Becket Church, he stated they had 170 children through the doors and 28 of them stayed for the whole hour, Cllr A Austin encouraged members to volunteer if they could. A discussion took place for the Clerk to look into DBS checks for members going to events such as this. • Cllr L Knight informed members that she had attended the Melodies in May concert at St Thomas a Becket Church on behalf of the Council and Mr Richard Hyde MBE asked her to say some closing remarks where Cllr L Knight promoted Bands on the Green. • Cllr V Fendley attended the U3A 15 th Anniversary event and informed members they had 236 members and 32 interest groups. • Cllr V Fendley informed members she had attended the St George’s Day Service in Huntingdon. • Cllr V Fendley informed Council that she represented Ramsey Town Council in place of Cllr C Maskell at the Local Visitor Economy Partnership and their next meeting on 14 th July will be in Ramsey. Cllr M Clarke asked for a minuted vote of thanks to the outgoing District Councillors, Cllr A Costello, Cllr J Clarke and Cllr S Corney for their dedication and hard work over many years. The Councillors had a round of applause.
231. Meeting Dates The next meeting of Ramsey Town Council (Planning) will take place on 28 th May 2026 at 7pm.

RAMSEY TOWN COUNCIL 
 
You are hereby summoned to attend a meeting of Ramsey Town Council to be held at 7pm 
on Thursday 11th June 2026, in The Lavender Room, Ramsey Town Council, Great 
Whyte, Ramsey, when the following items of business will be transacted: - 
 
Please ensure all mobile phones are switched off or turned to silent during the 
meeting. 
The meeting room will open to the public at 18.50. 
 
Lisa Renfree                                        5th June 2026 
   
  
 
  
Town Clerk/RFO 
 
A G E N D A  
 
 
APOLOGIES FOR ABSENCE 
 
1. DECLARATIONS OF INTEREST 
To receive declarations from Members as to disclosable pecuniary and other interests 
and the nature of those interests in relation to any agenda item. 
   
2. PUBLIC PARTICIPATION 
To allow 20 minutes for any members of the public to address the Council.  
 
3. MINUTES 
To approve as a correct record, the Minutes of the meeting of the Council held on 
28th May 2026 - attached. 
 
4. CO-OPTION OF NEW TOWN COUNCILLOR 
 
5. DISTRICT COUNCILLOR UPDATE: 
 
 
6. PLANNING 
• 1.1 26/008999/HHFUL Erection of single storey rear extension to dwelling – 56 
Hollow Lane, Ramsey. 
• 1.2 26/00931/FUL Use of land for two gypsy and traveller residential pitches (part 
retrospective). – One Acre Stables, Middle Drove, Ramsey Heights. 
• 1.3 26/00700/FUL Change of use of land to gypsy/traveller site and the erection of 
a shared dayroom (retrospective) – Land West of Goodliffe Cottage, Middle Drove, 
Ramsey Heights. 
 
 Planning – other business 
• To agree which one of the three independent assessors provided by HDC is to be 
used to legally review the Ramsey Communities Neighbourhood Plan. 
 
 
7. FINANCE ITEMS 
a) Financial Summary - Cash book to 31/5/26 to be noted– to be tabled. 

b) Expenditure Transactions to be approved– to be tabled. 
c) Year End Accounts – Presentation and approval of Year End Accounts and 
Annual Return to 31 March 2026 – attached 
 
 
8. POLICIES 
 To approve the Town Council’s draft IT Policy – attached. 
 To approve the draft Health and Safety Policy – attached. 
 
9. WORKING PARTY RECOMMENDATIONS 
Recommendations from the Amenities, Health and Leisure Working Party: 
• To use Proludic for the Newtown Road Play Park expansion. 
 
Recommendations from the Finance and Office Working Party: 
• To agree the £70 p/h cost for planning consultancy using Anthony Northcote 
Planning Ltd 
• To ringfence £5k of reserves to use for planning consultancy. 
• To agree Planning training for members at £22 per head 
• To carry out Enhanced DBS checks  
• To use Zurich for the annual insurance on a three-year programme £7272.00 per 
year 
• To consider an amount to assist with funding for the Ramsey Town Football club 
to move to a new location. 
• To approve a £4k budget to complete the Discover Ramsey website. 
 
10. TOWN MAYOR’S AND CLERK’S CORRESPONDENCE: 
• Update on Mews Car Park. 
 
11. ATTENDANCES AT MEETINGS AND ORGANISATIONS: 
 
 
12. MEETING DATES 
The next meeting of Ramsey Town Council will take place on 25th June 2026 at 7pm.  
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 

 
 
MINUTES OF RAMSEY TOWN COUNCIL MEETING 
held at 7pm on Thursday 28 May 2026  at  
Ramsey Town Council Great Whyte, Ramsey 
 
 
Present:  Councillors: I Axelsen, J Bufton, J Clarke, S Corney (Dep Mayor), A Costello, S Fice, V 
Fendley (Mayor), L Knight, C Maskell, and R Terrill. 
In attendance: Mrs Lisa Renfree, Town Clerk  
 
 
232. Apologies for Absence: Cllrs A Austin, J Aubin, M Clarke, P Rose and E Welsh.  
 
233.To Receive Declarations of Interest: There were no declarations at this point in the meeting, but 
Cllr J Bufton Knight declared a non-pecuniary interest in minute no.238 (4) a resident of Hollow Lane. 
 
234. Public  Participation: There  were  4  members  of  the  public  present,  District  Councillor  Cllr  H 
Tobias and Cllr K Maheshwari (arrived 7:15pm) and 2 residents.  
 
235. Minutes of the Last Meeting to be Approved: Proposed by Cllr S Corney and Seconded by Cllr 
S Fice, Council voted 10 FOR and 1 ABSTENTION to APPROVE the Minutes of the meeting of 14
th
 
May 2026 as a correct record. 
 
236.Nomination For Freedom of the Town. 
The nomination is for retired Councillor Mrs Pat Taylor. 
As you know Pat has been a long-standing member of council, serving twice as our Mayor once for a 
three-year term and then another for a two-year term and held the position of Deputy Mayor on 
several occasions. Mrs Taylor served from 14
th
 September 1989 and is well known for her work as a 
teacher at the Ailwyn as an English teacher. Proposed by Cllr A Costello and seconded by Cllr S 
Corney, Ramsey Town Council voted 10 FOR and 1 ABSTENTION (the member did not agree with 
these types of awards) for the Freedom of the Town to be awarded to Mrs Pat Taylor. 
 
237. Planning Applications for Consideration 
1.1 26/00761/FUL Conversion of two flats into three-bedroom house – 39 Great Whyte Ramsey. 
Proposed by Cllr S Corney and Cllr S Fice. Ramsey Town Council voted UNANIMOUSLY for the 
District Council to APPROVE the application. Members agreed it was the best for the property to turn 
back into a family home, has a driveway so no extra pressure on parking. 
 
1.2 26/00640/FUL Permanent use of land for 2 static caravans and 1 touring caravan for Gypsy and 
Traveller purposes.  Erection of dayroom building and associated works – Land on South Side of 
Middle Drove, Ramsey Heights. There was a large debate about this planning application and 
members want it noted that businesses are being run from down Middle Drove which is not permitted. 
The information given at the Development Management Committee on 16
th
 March about the distance 
to the local schools and shops was incorrect and also at that meeting it was said it had a good bus 
route- the bus has to go into Peterborough first so to get to Ramsey from Ramsey Heights via bus is a 
two-hour journey. Cllr V Fendley informed the members that the Neighbourhood Plan consultant has 
added an appendix to the document which outlines the restriction zones that impact the Nature 
Reserve and human sewage going into the waterways. The .gov site  
www.gov.uk/government/publications/planning-policy-for-traveller-sites/planning-policy-for-traveller-sites 
policy C was read out by the Clerk and Cllr A Costello read out policy E, Cllr S Fice also read out other 
sections from the document in particular point 13 flood risk which the site is 3A. Cllr J Clarke spoke 
about septic tanks are no longer permitted and need to be referred to as ‘klargester septic tanks’ 
Cllr V Fendley informed members that the two Freedom of Information requests to Huntingdonshire 
District Council and Cambridgeshire Police had not been responded to, the Clerk fed back that they 
had been chased up. It was noted that the Environment agency stated that the Internal Drainage 
Board had not made comment and Cllr J Clarke said he would be attending a meeting and would give 
feedback on this and ask for comment. Proposed by Cllr A Costello and seconded by Cllr S Fice, 
Ramsey Town Council voted UNANIMOUSLY for the District Council to REFUSE the application. 
There were no resident objections on the planning portal as they cannot redact their addresses and 

fear reprisals, but the following resident comments had been received by the Clerk and as previously 
been agreed with Huntingdonshire District Council they would be submitted by Ramsey Town 
Council.  
 
1) The landscape on both middle drove and harpers drove has changed dramatically over the last 7 yo 8 
years,  the countryside has been eroded away by concrete and static caravans and large chalet type buildings 
being placed  onto the fields that was once agricultural land, and the wildlife on the droves are being left with no 
habitat,  the view of the countryside has also changed over the last 7 to 8  years. 
 
2) sightings of Great crested newts have now been spotted on harpers drove very close to Uggmere Court Road 
and adjoining fields with middle drove,  we have now sent pictures to the great crested newts society and we are 
awaiting a site visit to extend the zone from walton fen nature reserve to Uggmere Court Road to protect them. 
 
3) The existing settled community on middle drove and school drove and harpers drove are not in balance with 
the traveller community and the existing settled community are now feeling that they have lost their own 
community and at times overwhelmed by the the large and ever growing traveller community that has already 
moved on to middle drove and harpers drove without any permission . 
 
4) The settled community are scared to challenge or voice their concerns to any anti social behaviour from the 
traveller community,  unable to call the police due to reprisals from the large community several residents have 
had property destroyed by the traveller community as a warning.  
 
5) Middle drove and harpers drove are now know as the crime capital of Ramsey,  this has made residents feel 
completely uneasy and ashamed to live in the ramsey heights area. 
 
6) The traveller community do not allow dogs into their homes as family pets , so they are housed outside in 
kennels, which leads to barking 24/7 , . 
 
7) The two community's are not compatible in such close proximity to each other its like two different world's 
have  collided.  
 
8) The volume of traffic that is now using the drove is causing the repairs to the drove to be carried out several 
times a year now , and the dust is causing residents to keep windows and doors closed.  
 
Below are just some of the anti social behaviours we have to contend with on a daily basis.  
 
 
1,tow trucks crashing over speed ramps day and night no consideration for residents.  
 
2, tree cutting services dropping waste from the backs of trucks , and left on the drove. 
 
3, scrap vehicles being transported down the gravel drove and dropping parts onto the drove. 
 
4, Off road motorbikes being driven at high speeds during the day and late into the evenings by children and 
adults.  
 
5, The burning of toxic materials during the day which means residents are unable to have washing out and have 
to have windows closed even during the hot summer months.  
 
6, speeding vehicles driven with no tax or insurance on the drove. 
 
7, The severe crime levels that now affect both droves , , 
 cannabis factory's being set up continuously, stolen vehicles,  stolen trailers,  stolen caravans,  stolen 
commercial vehicles, stolen tools,  
Traveller disputes taking place on the drove burnt-out tow trucks. 
 
8, The cutting into water supply and electricity.  
 
This is an honest opinion of how residents feel on middle drove and school drove and harpers drove and 
surrounding  

 
1.3 26/00642/FUL Permanent use for 1 mobile home and 1 touring caravan.  Erection of dayroom 
building and associated works – Land on South Side of Middle Drove, Ramsey Heights. After a long 
discussion which included noting the site was already there with temporary planning permission but 
now wanted permanent status and adding an extra dayroom which members commented was a 
bungalow minus a named bedroom, Proposed by Cllr A Costello and seconded by Cllr C Maskell, 
Ramsey Town Council voted 9 FOR and 1 ABSTENTION for the District Council to REFUSE the 
application. The comments previously submitted by the residents on 1.2 will also be submitted along 
with the Town Councils comments on overdevelopment of Gypsy / Traveller sites, no amenities, flood 
risk 3A, criminal activity. 
 
1.4 26/00752/FUL Change of use of land to mixed use Equestrian and Gypsy/Traveller site 
and the erection of a shared dayroom (retrospective) – Land Northwest of Two Acres, 
Middle Drove, Ramsey Heights. Proposed by Cllr S Corney and seconded by Cllr A 
Costello, Ramsey Town Council voted UNANIMOUSLEY for the District Council to 
REFUSE the application. It is overdevelopment in the countryside, and flood risk 3A. The 
comments from residents on 1.2 would also be submitted. 
1.5 26/00920/TREE Tree application – Tesco Stores Ltd, Neil Way, Ramsey. Proposed by Cllr S 
Corney and seconded by Cllr L Knight, Ramsey Town Council voted UNANIMOUSLY for the 
District Council to APPROVE the application and take the advice from the HDC Tree Officer. 
 
1.6 26/00481/HHFUL Single storey side extension and new driveway – 39 Station Road, Ramsey. 
Proposed by Cllr S Fice and seconded by Cllr L Knight, Ramsey Town Council vote 
UNANIMOUSLY for the District Council to APPROVE the application. Members noted the change 
of angle with the driveway and the updated comments from Cambridgeshire Highways. 
 
238. Planning Other Business: 
1- To be advised that Additional Sites Allocations for the Local Plan to 2046 will be 
available to view and comment between 13 May and 10 July. noted 
2- HDC have publicised that both The Ramsey Communities (Regulation 16) 
Neighbourhood Plan and The Giddings, Winwick and Hamerton (Reg 16) 
Neighbourhood Plan will be available to view and comment on between 11 May and 
23 June. noted 
3- Update on Ramsey Communities Neighbourhood Plan. Cllr V Fendley informed 
members that Huntingdonshire District Council had put forward two potential 
independent inspectors and we had been advised to ask for others and another name 
had been put forward. The NHP consultant would now do research and bring to the 
meeting for members to choose their preferred inspector. Cllr V Fendley informed the 
members that they look at areas of difference between the Ramsey Communities 
Neighbourhood Plan and the District Council Local Plan and they are the field between 
Ramsey Rural Museum and the 1940s Camp and the piece of land which David 
Wilson Homes was trying to build on between Ramsey and Bury. noted 
4- Abbey College Local Highways Initiative Bid (LHI). Members had tabled a plan of the 
speed cushions proposed in the Abbey College LHI bid and had been asked to 
comment on their positioning. After a detailed discussion and Cllr J Bufton spoke to 
members on his position of wanting no speed calming on Hollow Lane and felt the 
problems were caused by the lack of awareness of students themselves and that 
residents should not have to have speed cushions on the Lane all year round. Cllr J 
Clarke also asked that a comment went back to ensure the bus companies who 
transport the children were consulted for comment. Proposed by Cllr S Fice and 
seconded by Cllr S Corney Ramsey Town Council voted 7 FOR and 3 ABSTENTIONS 
for the following comments to be fed back to Abbey College Road Safety Group. 
Ramsey Town Council are pleased that speed cushion no.6 on the plan had been 
removed. They would ask the group to remove speed cushion 5 on the plan as they 
felt it would push the vehicles parking further up Hollow Lane and they would like the 
group to consider speed cushion 4 to be moved away from the junction and moved 

west. Ramsey Town Council would like the group to consult with the bus companies 
that transport the students for comment. 
 
 
239. Meeting Dates 
The next meeting of Ramsey Town Council will take place on 11th June 2026 at 7pm.

MINUTES OF RAMSEY TOWN COUNCIL MEETING held at 7pm on Thursday 28 May 2026  at Ramsey Town Council Great Whyte, Ramsey
Present:  Councillors: I Axelsen, J Bufton, J Clarke, S Corney (Dep Mayor), A Costello, S Fice, V Fendley (Mayor), L Knight, C Maskell, and R Terrill. In attendance: Mrs Lisa Renfree, Town Clerk

May 2026 as a correct record.

236.Nomination For Freedom of the Town. The nomination is for retired Councillor Mrs Pat Taylor. As you know Pat has been a long-standing member of council, serving twice as our Mayor once for a three-year term and then another for a two-year term and held the position of Deputy Mayor on several occasions. Mrs Taylor served from 14 th September 1989 and is well known for her work as a teacher at the Ailwyn as an English teacher. Proposed by Cllr A Costello and seconded by Cllr S Corney, Ramsey Town Council voted 10 FOR and 1 ABSTENTION (the member did not agree with these types of awards) for the Freedom of the Town to be awarded to Mrs Pat Taylor.

237. Planning Applications for Consideration 1.1 26/00761/FUL Conversion of two flats into three-bedroom house – 39 Great Whyte Ramsey. Proposed by Cllr S Corney and Cllr S Fice. Ramsey Town Council voted UNANIMOUSLY for the District Council to APPROVE the application. Members agreed it was the best for the property to turn back into a family home, has a driveway so no extra pressure on parking.

1.2 26/00640/FUL Permanent use of land for 2 static caravans and 1 touring caravan for Gypsy and Traveller purposes.  Erection of dayroom building and associated works – Land on South Side of Middle Drove, Ramsey Heights. There was a large debate about this planning application and members want it noted that businesses are being run from down Middle Drove which is not permitted. The information given at the Development Management Committee on 16 th March about the distance to the local schools and shops was incorrect and also at that meeting it was said it had a good bus route- the bus has to go into Peterborough first so to get to Ramsey from Ramsey Heights via bus is a two-hour journey. Cllr V Fendley informed the members that the Neighbourhood Plan consultant has added an appendix to the document which outlines the restriction zones that impact the Nature Reserve and human sewage going into the waterways. The .gov site www.gov.uk/government/publications/planning-policy-for-traveller-sites/planning-policy-for-traveller-sites policy C was read out by the Clerk and Cllr A Costello read out policy E, Cllr S Fice also read out other sections from the document in particular point 13 flood risk which the site is 3A. Cllr J Clarke spoke about septic tanks are no longer permitted and need to be referred to as ‘klargester septic tanks’ Cllr V Fendley informed members that the two Freedom of Information requests to Huntingdonshire District Council and Cambridgeshire Police had not been responded to, the Clerk fed back that they had been chased up. It was noted that the Environment agency stated that the Internal Drainage Board had not made comment and Cllr J Clarke said he would be attending a meeting and would give feedback on this and ask for comment. Proposed by Cllr A Costello and seconded by Cllr S Fice, Ramsey Town Council voted UNANIMOUSLY for the District Council to REFUSE the application. There were no resident objections on the planning portal as they cannot redact their addresses and
fear reprisals, but the following resident comments had been received by the Clerk and as previously been agreed with Huntingdonshire District Council they would be submitted by Ramsey Town Council.

1) The landscape on both middle drove and harpers drove has changed dramatically over the last 7 yo 8 years,  the countryside has been eroded away by concrete and static caravans and large chalet type buildings being placed  onto the fields that was once agricultural land, and the wildlife on the droves are being left with no habitat,  the view of the countryside has also changed over the last 7 to 8  years.

2) sightings of Great crested newts have now been spotted on harpers drove very close to Uggmere Court Road and adjoining fields with middle drove,  we have now sent pictures to the great crested newts society and we are awaiting a site visit to extend the zone from walton fen nature reserve to Uggmere Court Road to protect them.

3) The existing settled community on middle drove and school drove and harpers drove are not in balance with the traveller community and the existing settled community are now feeling that they have lost their own community and at times overwhelmed by the the large and ever growing traveller community that has already moved on to middle drove and harpers drove without any permission .

4) The settled community are scared to challenge or voice their concerns to any anti social behaviour from the traveller community,  unable to call the police due to reprisals from the large community several residents have had property destroyed by the traveller community as a warning.
5) Middle drove and harpers drove are now know as the crime capital of Ramsey,  this has made residents feel completely uneasy and ashamed to live in the ramsey heights area.
6) The traveller community do not allow dogs into their homes as family pets , so they are housed outside in kennels, which leads to barking 24/7 , .
7) The two community's are not compatible in such close proximity to each other its like two different world's have  collided.

8) The volume of traffic that is now using the drove is causing the repairs to the drove to be carried out several times a year now , and the dust is causing residents to keep windows and doors closed.
Below are just some of the anti social behaviours we have to contend with on a daily basis.
1,tow trucks crashing over speed ramps day and night no consideration for residents.
2, tree cutting services dropping waste from the backs of trucks , and left on the drove.
3, scrap vehicles being transported down the gravel drove and dropping parts onto the drove.
4, Off road motorbikes being driven at high speeds during the day and late into the evenings by children and adults.
5, The burning of toxic materials during the day which means residents are unable to have washing out and have to have windows closed even during the hot summer months.
6, speeding vehicles driven with no tax or insurance on the drove.

7, The severe crime levels that now affect both droves , , cannabis factory's being set up continuously, stolen vehicles,  stolen trailers,  stolen caravans,  stolen commercial vehicles, stolen tools, Traveller disputes taking place on the drove burnt-out tow trucks.
8, The cutting into water supply and electricity.
This is an honest opinion of how residents feel on middle drove and school drove and harpers drove and surrounding

1.3 26/00642/FUL Permanent use for 1 mobile home and 1 touring caravan.  Erection of dayroom building and associated works – Land on South Side of Middle Drove, Ramsey Heights. After a long discussion which included noting the site was already there with temporary planning permission but now wanted permanent status and adding an extra dayroom which members commented was a bungalow minus a named bedroom, Proposed by Cllr A Costello and seconded by Cllr C Maskell, Ramsey Town Council voted 9 FOR and 1 ABSTENTION for the District Council to REFUSE the application. The comments previously submitted by the residents on 1.2 will also be submitted along with the Town Councils comments on overdevelopment of Gypsy / Traveller sites, no amenities, flood risk 3A, criminal activity.

1.4 26/00752/FUL Change of use of land to mixed use Equestrian and Gypsy/Traveller site and the erection of a shared dayroom (retrospective) – Land Northwest of Two Acres, Middle Drove, Ramsey Heights. Proposed by Cllr S Corney and seconded by Cllr A Costello, Ramsey Town Council voted UNANIMOUSLEY for the District Council to REFUSE the application. It is overdevelopment in the countryside, and flood risk 3A. The comments from residents on 1.2 would also be submitted. 1.5 26/00920/TREE Tree application – Tesco Stores Ltd, Neil Way, Ramsey. Proposed by Cllr S Corney and seconded by Cllr L Knight, Ramsey Town Council voted UNANIMOUSLY for the District Council to APPROVE the application and take the advice from the HDC Tree Officer.

1.6 26/00481/HHFUL Single storey side extension and new driveway – 39 Station Road, Ramsey. Proposed by Cllr S Fice and seconded by Cllr L Knight, Ramsey Town Council vote UNANIMOUSLY for the District Council to APPROVE the application. Members noted the change of angle with the driveway and the updated comments from Cambridgeshire Highways.

238. Planning Other Business: 1- To be advised that Additional Sites Allocations for the Local Plan to 2046 will be available to view and comment between 13 May and 10 July. noted 2- HDC have publicised that both The Ramsey Communities (Regulation 16) Neighbourhood Plan and The Giddings, Winwick and Hamerton (Reg 16) Neighbourhood Plan will be available to view and comment on between 11 May and 23 June. noted 3- Update on Ramsey Communities Neighbourhood Plan. Cllr V Fendley informed members that Huntingdonshire District Council had put forward two potential independent inspectors and we had been advised to ask for others and another name had been put forward. The NHP consultant would now do research and bring to the meeting for members to choose their preferred inspector. Cllr V Fendley informed the members that they look at areas of difference between the Ramsey Communities Neighbourhood Plan and the District Council Local Plan and they are the field between Ramsey Rural Museum and the 1940s Camp and the piece of land which David Wilson Homes was trying to build on between Ramsey and Bury. noted 4- Abbey College Local Highways Initiative Bid (LHI). Members had tabled a plan of the speed cushions proposed in the Abbey College LHI bid and had been asked to comment on their positioning. After a detailed discussion and Cllr J Bufton spoke to members on his position of wanting no speed calming on Hollow Lane and felt the problems were caused by the lack of awareness of students themselves and that residents should not have to have speed cushions on the Lane all year round. Cllr J Clarke also asked that a comment went back to ensure the bus companies who transport the children were consulted for comment. Proposed by Cllr S Fice and seconded by Cllr S Corney Ramsey Town Council voted 7 FOR and 3 ABSTENTIONS for the following comments to be fed back to Abbey College Road Safety Group. Ramsey Town Council are pleased that speed cushion no.6 on the plan had been removed. They would ask the group to remove speed cushion 5 on the plan as they felt it would push the vehicles parking further up Hollow Lane and they would like the group to consider speed cushion 4 to be moved away from the junction and moved
west. Ramsey Town Council would like the group to consult with the bus companies that transport the students for comment.

held at 7pm on Thursday 9 July 2026 at

‘Although I am unable to attend this meeting, I would like to provide a brief update. 
I continue to hold regular meetings with constituents and remain accessible by email and through my social 
media channels, ensuring residents can contact me whenever they need assistance. 
Where issues raised by residents require the involvement of Ramsey Town Council, I copy the Town Council 
into the relevant correspondence so that matters can be dealt with collaboratively. 
Since the last Town Council meeting, no issues have been referred to me by Ramsey Town Council that require 
an update. However, I remain available to assist the Town Council, fellow councillors and residents whenever 
support is needed. Please do not hesitate to contact me if there are any district council matters on which I can 
help. 
Thank you, and I look forward to continuing to work together for the benefit of Ramsey and the surrounding 
communities. 
Thanks 
Kind regards 
Cllr Karan Maheshwari

Huntingdonshire District Council and asked the Clerk to raise this with them. Further feedback was that in Cllr 
Maheshwari report he stated he had not been asked to do any work on behalf of Ramsey Town Council, Cllr S 
Corney reminded members that he been asked to speak to Huntingdonshire District Council about the land at 
the back of the Doctors Surgery on Mews Close, and that Cllr S Corney had spoken to him at length after the

th
 July Party in the Park a Town Council event. The 
Clerk had been asked to correspond with the three District Councillors for clarity on these issues and to gain 
commitment for future meetings.

1.1  26/01152/OUT Proposed  outline  application  for  development  of  up  to  19  residential  dwellings  with  matters 
committed  to  access.  Hankins  Garage  46  Whytefield Road.  Ramsey  PE26  1AH.After  a  lengthy  discussion 
Proposed by Cllr L Webster and seconded by Cllr S Fice Ramsey Town Council voted UNANIMOUSLY for the 
District Council to APPROVE the outline plan but wanted the following comments to be noted for further plans.  
Ramsey Town Council members suggested the following: 
• having a lesser number of houses on the plot and increase the number of car parking spaces.  
• To have allocated visitor parking to take pressure away from Whytefield Road.  
• Have concerns where the flow of the attenuation pond would flow to 

• Suggest bungalow housing maybe preferable and take pressure away from parking spaces required. 
• There  is  a  strip  of  land  that  goes  from  the  site  to  Blenheim  Road  and  even  though  it  is  outside  of  the 
application boundary was assurance this would not be used for traffic. 
• Council felt the application should make S106 and CIL contribution.

a)  TRO – pedestrianisation – The  Clerk  informed members  that  the  TRO  was  now  being  looked  at  by 
Cambridgeshire Highways and work should start in September.

Ramsey Town Council, Cllr V Fendley reminded Members that the Ramsey Communities Neighbourhood Plan

Cemetery Working Party 
For Council to agree to explore the option of having green burials in the Cemetery Extension, working in 
partnership with Muchwood. Cllr M Clarke informed members of the discussion that had taken place with

public. This is now being investigated by Cambridgeshire Police. Cllr A Austin reminded the Clerk that if she 
requires immediate support to call the Emergency What’s App and a member would come to support. The Clerk 
along with council staff have access to a panic button as part of the Lone Working Policy. It was agreed the 
situation would be monitored.

a) Cllr H Tobias email to the Clerk and response – Council to consider if any further comments are required – 
letter previously circulated. The Clerk had previously circulated an email and response that she had received 
from Huntingdonshire District Councillor for Ramsey Cllr Howard Tobias. The Clerk was instructed to write a 
further letter to Cllr H Tobais explaining the legislation that Town Council follow and cannot raise funds for other 
public bodies, to advise Cllr H Tobias to have a meeting with the Police and Crime Commissioner Daryl Preston 
who can influence where funds are spent on Policing. The Clerk was also asked to reiterate that the offer to use 
the facilities of Ramsey Town Council, the library was still available and to explore the use of the Ramsey Fire 
Station. 

 
b) Parking on Abbey Road. The Clerk informed Council that residents of Abbey Road had expressed concern 
over the parking plans at Abbey College. They were currently suffering from excess parking outside their 
properties and wanted to know what they could do. The Clerk had spoken with them and given advice. Cllr J 
Clarke did not think the road was private as the council had adopted the road from Hollow Lane to the Last 
house. Cllr J Bufton thought the bus turn around and the road to the school could be private and belong to the 
school. Cllr J Bufton suggested we note the residents’ comments but knowing that there will always have 
parking in Abbey Road because the school shut the gates for a short period of time each day.  
 
265. Freedom of Information Request from Ramsey Town Council 
FOI received from Huntingdonshire District Council this had previously been circulated to members and whilst 
they were disappointed in the response no further action would take place at this time. 
FOI Cambridgeshire Police – a response had now been received and would be circulated to members.

able to meet many other dignitaries from Cambridgeshire. 
• The Clerk fed back from the 4
th
 July event, saying the feedback was, more please, and that ideas had 
been given for future event.

Community Assets, they must still follow process and not sell the assets cheaply as it could impact the 
new Unitary. CIL can still be awarded even if it is for a future project and the funds can be ring-fenced.

than one hundred plus residents of all ages.

enterprise.

the extra showing funded by Ramsey Town Council other groups including the Brownies attended
