Replace the third paragraph of the policy with the following: “Development proposals will be supported where they can demonstrate that there is capacity in the local surface water drainage system, the water supply network and the sewerage network, or capacity can be made available in time to support the development, having regard to the advice of Anglian Water.” PM6 Page 88 In the third paragraph of Policy 8, following reference to a network of walking and cycling linkages, add a footnote referencing the Ramsey Market Town Transport Strategy. Add an extract from the Strategy to the Neighbourhood Plan. RAMSEY TOWN COUNCIL 
 
You are hereby summoned to attend a meeting of Ramsey Town Council to be held at 7pm 
on Thursday 10th September 2026, in The Lavender Room, Ramsey Town Council, 
Great Whyte, Ramsey, when the following items of business will be transacted: - 
 
Please ensure all mobile phones are switched off or turned to silent during the 
meeting. 
The meeting room will open to the public at 18.50. 
 
Lisa Renfree                                      4th September 2026 
   
  
 
  
Town Clerk/RFO 
 
A G E N D A  
 
 
APOLOGIES FOR ABSENCE 
 
1. DECLARATIONS OF INTEREST 
To receive declarations from Members as to disclosable pecuniary and other 
interests and the nature of those interests in relation to any agenda item. 
   
2. PUBLIC PARTICIPATION 
    To allow 20 minutes for any members of the public to address the Council.  
 
3. MINUTES 
To approve as a correct record, the Minutes of the meeting of the Council held on 
27
th
 August 2026 - attached. 
 
4. DISTRICT & COUNTY COUNCILLOR UPDATE: 
Cllrs H Tobias, K Maheshwari and R Coogan have been invited to address Town 
Council Members. 
 
5. PLANNING 
1.1 26/01440/FUL Change of use to a SEN day school (Class F1), erection of a 
rear single storey extension, external alterations to existing two-storey rear 
extension and associated works including additional car parking, new 
landscaping and recreation areas – Westward House, Bury Road, Ramsey. 
1.2 26/01089/HHFUL Proposed replacement roof to form first floor 
accommodation, demolition of the existing porch and erection of a new single 
storey porch, erection of a new balcony, installation of external insulation and 
cladding to the existing dwelling and associated internal alterations – Living 
Accommodation Stokes Garage, Ramsey Road, Ramsey Forty Foot. 
 
 
 Planning – other business 
a) Local Plan 2047 - Update  
b) Neighbourhood Plan Independent Inspector Report Update. 
 
 

6. FINANCE ITEMS 
a) Financial Summary - Cash book to 31/8/26 to be noted– to be tabled. 
b) Expenditure Transactions to be approved– to be tabled. 
c) To approve the implementation of the Local Government Pay Award - Pay rates 
and allowances have been increased by 3.3% with effect from 1
st
 April 2026.  
d) Updated Grant Form  
 
  
7. FUTURE SCOOTER PERMISSION 
Future Scooter would like to hold one to one training session on the QEII Skate 
Park and are seeking permission from Ramsey Town Council. 
 
 
8. WORKING PARTY UPDATES  
Members to receive an update from the Chair of each Working Party- circulated, to 
be noted. 
 
Communications Working Party 
Recommendation: 
Draft newsletter - to be tabled 
 
9. TOWN MAYOR’S AND CLERK’S CORRESPONDENCE: 
a) Just Giving Fire Fighter Fund Update 
b) FOI Response on CIL Funding Update. 
c) Emergency Planning Meeting – 1
st
 October 6:30pm at Ramsey Community 
Centre. 
d) Climate Emergency Briefing- 23
rd
 September at St Thomas a Becket Church 
6pm. 
e) Council to decide on centralised headstones in the lawn cemetery 
 
10. ATTENDANCES AT MEETINGS AND ORGANISATIONS: 
a) 1940 Drumhead Service 
b) Heritage Day – Councillor Support. 
 
11. DISTRICT WIDE DOG PSPO RENEWAL – CONSULTATION,  
Council to respond. 
 
12. MEETING DATES 
The next meeting of Ramsey Town Council (Planning) will take place on 24th 
September 2026 at 7pm.  
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 

MINUTES OF RAMSEY TOWN COUNCIL MEETING 
held at 7pm on Thursday 27 August 2026 at  
Ramsey Town Council Great Whyte, Ramsey 
 
 
Present:  Councillors: I Axelsen, J Bufton, J Clarke, M Clarke, V Fendley (Mayor), S Fice, R Terrill, J 
Thompson, and  L Webster. 
In attendance: Mrs A Jerrom, Deputy Town Clerk  
 
The Chairman welcomed new Councillor Jessie Thompson to the meeting. 
 
289. Apologies for Absence. 
Cllrs J Aubin, A Austin, S Corney, A Costello, L Knight, C Maskell and P Rose. 
 
290.To Receive Declarations of Interest. 
No declarations of interest were made. 
 
291. Public Participation. 
There were no members of the public present. 
 
292. Minutes of the Last Meeting to be Approved. 
Councillors voted with two abstentions to accept the Minutes of the meeting of the Council held on 13
th
 
August 2026 as a correct record. 
 
293. Planning Applications for Consideration. 
1.1 26/01416/HHFUL – Two storey extension, barn and carport, internal and external alterations, new 
dormer and canopy roofs and installation of solar PV panels – Heathfield, Benwick Road, Ramsey Forty 
Foot    Proposed  by  Cllr  S  Fice  and  seconded  by  Cllr  L  Webster  Ramsey  Town  Council  voted 
unanimously for Huntingdonshire District Council to APPROVE the application as per their decision on 
a previous application for the property in June 2026, which had since been withdrawn. 
1.2  26/01206/OUT – Proposed demolition of an existing dwelling and outbuilding and replacement with 
4 new dwellings (outline application with all matters reserved, with the exception of access) – 190 Herne 
Road, Ramsey St Marys.  Having been proposed by Cllr J Clarke and seconded by Cllr Terrill, councillors 
voted  unanimously  to  recommend  refusal  of  the  application  due  to  the  lack  of  information  regarding 
adequate parking, particularly for the bungalows at the rear of the development.  They also had concerns 
regarding the possible precedent that might be set for development at the rear of properties in the village. 
1.3 26/01484/TREE – G1  (dead  Silver  Birch) – fell  and  remove – Cedar  Lodge,  St  Marys  Road, 
Ramsey.  Having  been  proposed  by  Cllr  S  Fice  and  seconded  by  Cllr  L  Webster  councillors  voted 
unanimously to make no observations either in favour or against the proposal but to leave the decision 
to the arboricultural officer. 
 
294.  Consultation on the Reviewed Bury Draft Neighbourhood Plan. 
Councillors discussed the suggested response to the consultation previously circulated by Cllr Fendley. 
It was agreed that there would be infrastructure implications for Ramsey following the growth within the 
Bury Neighbourhood Plan area. It was therefore proposed by Cllr Bufton, seconded by Cllr Terrill and 
agreed with one abstention to submit that response from the Town Council which included the 
acknowledgment of the need for Infrastructure Levy(CIL) contributions towards car parking provision at 
Mews Close and electric charging points which would serve the wider community. 
 
 
 
295. Update on Emergency Response – Holme Fen. 
Councillor Fendley provided an update on the huge operation to support the Fire Service while they 
were attending the recent fires at Holme Fen.  In answer to a request for emergency assistance from 
HDC the Mayor and Town Clerk had organised for food supplies to be provided to the firemen 
alongside that already organised by the Admiral Wells in Holme and Cllr Fendley had set up a Go 
Fund Me page for donations. There had been an amazing response from the community, with 
volunteers and local businesses providing food over the weekend and following days.  Cllr Fendley 
reported that the firemen had been overwhelmed by the response and hard work of all concerned and 
they would be issuing formal letters of thanks. There would be a further update on the Go Fund Me 

funds at the next meeting of the Town Council.  The Chief Fire Officer had been invited to attend the 
Mayor’s Civic Service in September. 
 
296. Meeting Dates 
The next meeting of Ramsey Town Council would take place on Thursday 10th September at 7pm.

MINUTES OF RAMSEY TOWN COUNCIL MEETING 
held at 7pm on Thursday 27 August 2026 at  
Ramsey Town Council Great Whyte, Ramsey 
 
 
Present:  Councillors: I Axelsen, J Bufton, J Clarke, M Clarke, V Fendley (Mayor), S Fice, R 
Terrill, J Thompson, and  L Webster. 
In attendance: Mrs A Jerrom, Deputy Town Clerk  
 
The Chairman welcomed new Councillor Jessie Thompson to the meeting. 
 
289. Apologies for Absence. 
Cllrs J Aubin, A Austin, S Corney, A Costello, L Knight, C Maskell and P Rose. 
 
290.To Receive Declarations of Interest. 
No declarations of interest were made. 
 
291. Public Participation. 
There were no members of the public present. 
 
292. Minutes of the Last Meeting to be Approved. 
Councillors  voted with  two  abstentions to  accept  the Minutes  of the meeting  of the  Council 
held on 13
th
 August 2026 as a correct record. 
 
293. Planning Applications for Consideration. 
1.1 26/01416/HHFUL – Two  storey extension,  barn and  carport,  internal  and  external 
alterations,  new  dormer and  canopy  roofs  and  installation  of  solar  PV  panels – Heathfield, 
Benwick Road, Ramsey Forty Foot  Proposed by Cllr S Fice and seconded by Cllr L Webster 
Ramsey Town Council voted unanimously for Huntingdonshire District Council to APPROVE 
the application as per their decision on a previous application for the property in June 2026, 
which had since been withdrawn. 
1.2  26/01206/OUT – Proposed  demolition  of  an  existing  dwelling  and  outbuilding  and 
replacement  with  4  new  dwellings  (outline  application with  all  matters  reserved,  with  the 
exception of access) – 190 Herne Road, Ramsey St Marys.  Having been proposed by Cllr J 
Clarke and seconded by Cllr Terrill, councillors voted unanimously to recommend refusal of the 
application  due  to  the  lack  of information  regarding adequate parking,  particularly  for  the 
bungalows  at  the  rear  of  the  development.    They  also had  concerns  regarding  the  possible 
precedent that might be set for development at the rear of properties in the village. 
1.3 26/01484/TREE – G1  (dead  Silver  Birch) – fell  and remove – Cedar  Lodge,  St Marys 
Road,  Ramsey. Having  been  proposed  by  Cllr  S  Fice  and  seconded  by  Cllr  L  Webster 
councillors voted unanimously to make no observations either in favour or against the proposal 
but to leave the decision to the arboricultural officer. 
 
294.  Consultation on the Reviewed Bury Draft Neighbourhood Plan. 
Councillors discussed the suggested response to the consultation previously circulated by 
Cllr Fendley. It was agreed that there would be infrastructure implications for Ramsey 
following the growth within the Bury Neighbourhood Plan area. It was therefore proposed by 
Cllr Bufton, seconded by Cllr Terrill and agreed with one abstention to submit that response 
from the Town Council which included the acknowledgment of the need for Infrastructure 
Levy(CIL) contributions towards car parking provision at Mews Close and electric charging 
points which would serve the wider community. 
 
 
 

2 
 
295. Update on Emergency Response – Holme Fen. 
Councillor Fendley provided an update on the huge operation to support the Fire Service 
while they were attending the recent fires at Holme Fen.  In answer to a request for 
emergency assistance from HDC the Mayor and Town Clerk had organised for food supplies 
to be provided to the firemen alongside that already organised by the Admiral Wells in Holme 
and Cllr Fendley had set up a Go Fund Me page for donations. There had been an amazing 
response from the community, with volunteers and local businesses providing food over the 
weekend and following days.  Cllr Fendley reported that the firemen had been overwhelmed 
by the response and hard work of all concerned and they would be issuing formal letters of 
thanks. There would be a further update on the Go Fund Me funds at the next meeting of the 
Town Council.  The Chief Fire Officer had been invited to attend the Mayor’s Civic Service in 
September. 
 
296. Meeting Dates 
The next meeting of Ramsey Town Council would take place on Thursday 10th September 
at 7pm.

news.title: Community Praise Following Holme Fen Fires Emergency Response
news.summary: Ramsey Town Council praised the overwhelming community response and local businesses in supporting firefighters during the recent fires at Holme Fen.
news.content: Cllr Fendley provided an update on the operation to support the Fire Service during recent fires at Holme Fen. The Mayor and Town Clerk organised food supplies alongside the Admiral Wells in Holme, and a Go Fund Me page was set up. Volunteers and local businesses provided food over the weekend, leaving firefighters overwhelmed by the community response. Formal letters of thanks are to be issued, and the Chief Fire Officer has been invited to the Mayor's Civic Service in September.

governance.title: Planning Applications Recommendations
governance.summary: Council voted to recommend approval for a two-storey extension, barn, and solar PV panels at Heathfield, Benwick Road, Ramsey Forty Foot; recommended refusal for 4 new dwellings at 190 Herne Road, Ramsey St Marys due to parking concerns and precedent; and made no observations on a tree-felling application at Cedar Lodge, St Marys Road, Ramsey.

governance.title: Bury Draft Neighbourhood Plan Consultation Response
governance.summary: Agreed to submit a consultation response highlighting infrastructure implications for Ramsey from growth in the Bury Neighbourhood Plan area, requesting Infrastructure Levy (CIL) contributions for car parking at Mews Close and electric charging points.

MINUTES OF RAMSEY TOWN COUNCIL MEETING 
held at 7pm on Thursday 13 August 2026 at  
Ramsey Town Council Great Whyte, Ramsey 
 
 
Present:  Councillors: I Axelsen, J Clarke, M Clarke, S Corney (Dep Mayor), A Costello, V 
Fendley (Mayor), L Knight, C Maskell, R Terrill, L Webster, and E Welsh. 
In attendance: Mrs L Renfree, Town Clerk  
274. Apologies for Absence. 
Cllrs J Aubin, A Austin, J Bufton, S Fice, and P Rose. 
 
275.To Receive Declarations of Interest. 
No declarations of interest were received. 
 
276. Public Participation. 
There were 10 members of the public present. 
 
277. Minutes of the Last Meeting to be Approved. 
To approve as a correct record, the minutes of the meeting Council held on 23rd July 2026, 
previously circulated. Proposed by Cllr S Corney and seconded by Cllr R Terrill Ramsey Town 
Council voted UNANIMOUSLY to accept the minutes of 23rd July as a true record. 
 
278. Co-option of New Town Councillor. 
Three  candidates  put  themselves  forward  for  co-option,  each  applicant  addressed  the 
members giving an overview of themselves and why they felt they would be a good addition 
to the Town Council. The members voted and Jessie Thompson received the most votes and 
would join the council at their August planning meeting. 
 
279. District and County Councillor Update: 
Cllrs Coogan, Maheshwari and Tobias were invited to update members of District and County 
Council matters, apologies received from Cllr R Coogan, and a report tabled to members. No 
apologies from Cllr Maheshwari. Cllr Tobias reported back in person at the meeting as follows: 
Cllr  Tobias  informed members  that  he  does  not  use  social  media  to  conduct  his  council 
business  both  at  District  and  County  level  and is  looking  to  work in collaboration with  the 
council and residents, listening and challenging to make the Ramsey ward a better place to 
be. Since the Huntingdonshire District Council meeting Cllr Tobias had been looking into the 
parking assessment and challenging the fact there is no business case for spending £370,000 
of taxpayer’s money.  Cllr  Tobias  informed  members  that  some  Ramsey  plans  were  being 
discussed at the next Development Management Committee meeting. Cllr Tobias was happy 
to  support  CIL (Community  Infrastructure  Levy)  applications  if  they  will  support  the  wider 
community. From a County Council perspective Cllr Tobias had been in the role for 28 days 
and  had  planned  to  meet Highways  looking  at  the  road  infrastructure  and  is  looking  at  the 
Student Bus situation where the decision was made by the Peterborough College. The Clerk 
was asked to communicate with Cllr Tobias to continue the work asked of Cllr Maheshwari on 
securing the land for the car park on Mews Close. 
 
280. Planning Applications for Consideration 
1.1 26/01128/LBC – Injection of a SecoMUR chemical damp proof course into drilled holes to 
all external walls and solid brick internal walls- Bridge Farm 15 Ramsey Road, Ramsey Forty 
Foot. Proposed by Cllr S Corney and seconded by Cllr M Clarke Ramsey Town Council voted 
UNANIMOUSLY for Huntingdonshire District Council to APPROVE the application. 
1.2  26/01328/HHFUL – Replacement  of  damaged  cladding to  front,  side  and  rear  of  the 
property- 17 Wyatt Close, Ramsey. Proposed by Cllr S Corney and seconded by L Webster 
Ramsey   Town   Council   voted UNANIMOUSLY for   Huntingdonshire   District   Council   to 

2 
 
APPROVE the  application,  there  was  neighbouring  support  for  the application, and  it  is  in 
keeping with the area. 
1.3 26/01385/FUL- Change of use of land from agricultural to residential curtilage associated 
with Kingfisher House – Kingfisher House, Whittlesey Road, Benwick, March. Proposed by 
Cllr C Maskell and seconded by Cllr J Clarke Ramsey Town Council voted UNANIMOUSLY 
for Huntingdonshire District Council to APPROVE the application. 
1.4 26/01352/FUL – Change of use of land to a gypsy and traveller residential pitch 
comprising the siting of one mobile home, one amenity building, associated hardstanding 
and ancillary works (part retrospective). – Land East of Fern Cottage, Harpers Drove, 
Ramsey Heights. The Clerk had received objections to the application from residents of 
Ramsey Heights as previously agreed with Huntingdonshire District Council. The Clerk 
was asked to submit to the planning portal their objections as laid out in the 21-page 
report previously circulated. Cllr A Costello proposed REFUSAL and Cllr seconded by 
Cllr L Webster Ramsey Town Council voted UNANIMOUSLY for the District Council to 
REFUSE this application. The Clerk would also put the residents comments to the 
planning portal. 
 
281. Planning Other Business: 
a) Pedestrianisation update: Cllr V Fendley informed members that the TRO was live and 
that there would be a planning application being submitted for the shop in a box units. 
b) Abbey College LHI BID- The plans were out for consultation and Ramsey Town 
Council were asked if they wanted to add any further comments on the plan. Ramsey 
Town Council did not want to add any further comments. 
c) Consultation on the Reviewed Bury Village Draft Neighbourhood Plan – Cllr V Fendley 
talked through the Goals and Objectives from the Bury Village Neighbourhood Plan 
and informed members it would be on the agenda for the next planning meeting for 
comment. 
d) To note the Tree Preservation Order26/002 – Ramsey Rural Museum had been 
confirmed. Noted 
e) Notice of application for a Town/ Village Green, Abbey Green, Ramsey. Noted. 
f) Huntingdonshire District Council Local Plan Consultation – Members to agree to using 
Anthony Northcote for advice regarding Ramsey Town Council’s response. Proposed 
by Cllr L Knight and seconded by Cllr R Terrill Ramsey town Council voted 10 FOR and 
1 AGAINST for the Clerk to instruct Anthony Northcote to give advice to Ramsey Town 
Council to comment on Huntingdonshire District Council’s Local Plan. 
282. Finance Items: 
a) Financial Summary – Cash book to 31/07/2026 tabled – Noted 
b) Expenditure Transactions to be approved – tabled- Proposed by Cllr S Corney and 
seconded by Cllr L Knight Ramsey Town Council voted UNANIMOUSLY to agree the 
expenditure transactions. 
283. Working Part Recommendations: 
 Recommendations from the Economic Development Working Party 
a) For Ramsey Town Council to agree in principle to take control of the shop in a box 
units moving forward post successful TRO and Full Planning approval, and for 
Ramsey Town Council to manage the gated timings – Proposed by Cllr L Knight and 
seconded by Cllr S Corney Ramsey Town Council voted 10 FOR and 1 ABSTENTION 
for Ramsey Town Council to in principle take control of the Shop in a box units subject 
to a successful TRO and Full Planning approval. Proposed by Cllr L Knight and 

3 
 
seconded by Cllr S Corney Ramsey Town Council voted 10 FOR and 1 ABSTENTION 
for Ramsey Town Council to manage the gated timings. 
b) For Ramsey Town Council to initiate a Local Business Group to engage with our local 
businesses, with a view to sharing information. It was felt that a communication 
streamline to all Ramsey Parish Businesses was lacking and that this meeting would 
bring them together to explore a process moving forward. Proposed by Cllr L Knight 
and seconded by Cllr S Corney Ramsey Town Council voted UNANIMOUSLY for a 
business meeting to be arranged in September. 
Recommendations from the Amenities, Highways, Health, and Leisure Working 
Party. 
a) For Ramsey Town Council to decide between two quotes for the Public Toilet Doors 
both quotes ex vat. The quote covers three new doors: Healthmatic £8040 or LAM 
Automation Ltd £8660 – The Clerk made an amendment to the cost of the 
Healthmatic quote £10,050. Proposed by Cllr A Costello and seconded by Cllr C 
Maskell Ramsey Town Council voted UNANIMOUSLY to accept the quote from LAM 
Automation LTD at a cost of £8,660.00 and the funds would come from the CIL 
account.  
b) For Ramsey Town Council to decide if they want the public toilet doors to have 
windows in them at a cost of £700 ex vat. Proposed by Cllr J Clarke and seconded by 
Cllr C Maskell to REFUSE the windows in the public toilet doors. Ramsey Town 
Council voted REFUSE 6 and 3 AGAINST 2 ABSTENTIONS for the public toilets to 
not have windows. 
c) For Ramsey Town Council to agree in principle a large mural sited at the QEII 
Skatepark. Final design to be voted on in the future. - paper circulated. After a long 
discussion on the subject, it was agreed UNANIMOUSLY for the proposal to go back 
to Amenities, Highways, Health & Leisure for further exploration. 
Recommendations from the Communications Working Party. 
      a) To Agree the draft Digital Screen Policy for Ramsey Town Council previously                                                                                       
circulated. Proposed by Cllr L Knight and seconded by Cllr S Corney Ramsey Town Council 
voted 10 FOR and 1 ABSTENTION to APPROVE the Digital Screen Policy. 
a) To Agree the Risk Assessment for Public Meetings at Ramsey Town Council- 
previously circulated. Proposed by Cllr L Knight and seconded by Cllr S 
Corney. Ramsey Town Council voted 9 FOR and 2 ABSTENTIONS to 
APPROVE the Risk Assessment for Public Meetings. 
b) To Agree the Risk Assessment for Premises and Buildings- previously 
circulated. Proposed by Cllr L Knight and seconded by Cllr S Corney Ramsey 
Town Council vote 9 FOR and 2 ABSTENTIONS to APPROVE the Risk 
Assessment for Premises and Buildings. 
c) To Review the current IT Policy – previously circulated. Proposed by Cllr L 
Knight and seconded by Cllr S Corney Ramsey Town Council voted 10 FOR 
and 1 ABSTENTION to APPROVE the updated IT Policy. 
d) To agree the new email footer –tabled. Proposed by Cllr L Knight and 
seconded by Cllr S Corney Ramsey Town Council vote 10 FOR and 1 
ABSTENTION to use the footer tabled for Councillor emails. The Clerk will 
circulate to members to use. 
284. WORKING PARTY UPDATE  
a) Members to receive an update from the Chair of each Working Party- 
previously circulated. Cllr L Knight said this was a very useful document and is 
a really good idea. The document was noted. 
 
285. FEEDBACK FROM GRANT FROM COMMUNITY SAFETY & 
SAFETY PARTNERSHIP. 

4 
 
a) Feedback from Future Scooter Foundation -the Clerk showed two small video 
clips from some of the young people who participated in the evening event. 
There was a positive debate, and it was agreed that it would be good to have 
more young girls participating. Noted 
 
286. TOWN MAYOR’S AND CLERK’S CORRESPONDENCE: 
a) Update on Anti-Social Behaviour on the Clerk and Council. The Clerk updated 
members on the investigation with Huntingdonshire District Council Anti-Social 
behaviour team. They are now looking to produce a Criminal Behaviour Order 
to protect the Council. 
b) Resident communication on noise from skate park and concerns RTC would 
put lighting there for after dark use. The Clerk informed members that a 
resident after reading a District Councillors post on having lighting at the 
Skatepark was very upset as Ramsey Town Council had said that would not 
be the case. Cllr Fendley was very clear that there would be no plans to light 
up the Skatepark. 
c) Resident communication on thanking the Town Council for the work Paul and 
Morgan are doing keeping the Cemetery clear and improving the area. The 
Clerk informed members that positive comments had been received about the 
work in clearing the Cemetery. 
d) Thank you from the Ramsey Garden and Horticulture Club for the grant we 
gave them which enable two new competitions this year. Cllr Fendley informed 
members of the letter received thanking Ramsey Town Council for their grant 
and the opportunities it has given their club. 
e) Ramsey Heights residents concern over lack of Fire Hydrant for the Droves. 
After the fire on Harpers Drove, residents were concerned that the Fire Service 
had to keep going away to refill the tanker. This was noted. 
Councillor Costello left the meeting at 8:55pm. 
287. ATTENDANCES AT MEETINGS AND ORGANISATIONS: 
a) Safer Communities Public Meeting - Cllr V Fendley fed back on the public 
meeting held at Ramsey Forty Foot. Cllr V Fendley praised the Inspector for 
his honesty during the meeting, but the overall outcome was we do live in a 
safe community. 
b) Mayor met with County Councillor Cllr H Tobias. Cllr V Fendley informed 
members that she had had a meeting and discussed the LHI bids and 
infrastructure. 
c) Magnolia Park Opening Day- Cllr V Fendley attended the opening and it was a 
very positive day. 
d) Jones Court 40
th
 Anniversary BBQ – Cllr V Fendley and the Clerk attended the 
BBQ, and Cllr V Fendley had the difficult task of judging the baking 
competition. 
e) Update on correspondence with Cambridgeshire Constabulary – Cllr R Terrill 
updated members on his conversation with Inspector Norden. 
f) MP Sam Carling – Local Surgery Date 14
th
 August 2026. Cllr V Fendley 
informed members that the MP was in the community meeting with residents. 
 
288. MEETING DATES 
The next meeting of Ramsey Town Council (Planning) will take place on 27th August 
2026 at 7pm.

Proposed by Cllr L Knight and seconded by Cllr R Terrill Ramsey town Council voted 10 FOR and 1 AGAINST for the Clerk to instruct Anthony Northcote to give advice to Ramsey Town Council to comment on Huntingdonshire District Council’s Local Plan. 282. Finance Items: a) Financial Summary – Cash book to 31/07/2026 tabled – Noted b) Expenditure Transactions to be approved – tabled- Proposed by Cllr S Corney and seconded by Cllr L Knight Ramsey Town Council voted UNANIMOUSLY to agree the expenditure transactions. 283. Working Part Recommendations: Recommendations from the Economic Development Working Party a) For Ramsey Town Council to agree in principle to take control of the shop in a box units moving forward post successful TRO and Full Planning approval, and for Ramsey Town Council to manage the gated timings – Proposed by Cllr L Knight and seconded by Cllr S Corney Ramsey Town Council voted 10 FOR and 1 ABSTENTION for Ramsey Town Council to in principle take control of the Shop in a box units subject to a successful TRO and Full Planning approval. Proposed by Cllr L Knight and

seconded by Cllr S Corney Ramsey Town Council voted 10 FOR and 1 ABSTENTION for Ramsey Town Council to manage the gated timings. b) For Ramsey Town Council to initiate a Local Business Group to engage with our local businesses, with a view to sharing information. It was felt that a communication streamline to all Ramsey Parish Businesses was lacking and that this meeting would bring them together to explore a process moving forward. Proposed by Cllr L Knight and seconded by Cllr S Corney Ramsey Town Council voted UNANIMOUSLY for a business meeting to be arranged in September. Recommendations from the Amenities, Highways, Health, and Leisure Working Party. a) For Ramsey Town Council to decide between two quotes for the Public Toilet Doors both quotes ex vat. The quote covers three new doors: Healthmatic £8040 or LAM Automation Ltd £8660 – The Clerk made an amendment to the cost of the Healthmatic quote £10,050. Proposed by Cllr A Costello and seconded by Cllr C Maskell Ramsey Town Council voted UNANIMOUSLY to accept the quote from LAM Automation LTD at a cost of £8,660.00 and the funds would come from the CIL account. b) For Ramsey Town Council to decide if they want the public toilet doors to have windows in them at a cost of £700 ex vat. Proposed by Cllr J Clarke and seconded by Cllr C Maskell to REFUSE the windows in the public toilet doors. Ramsey Town Council voted REFUSE 6 and 3 AGAINST 2 ABSTENTIONS for the public toilets to not have windows. c) For Ramsey Town Council to agree in principle a large mural sited at the QEII Skatepark. Final design to be voted on in the future. - paper circulated. After a long discussion on the subject, it was agreed UNANIMOUSLY for the proposal to go back to Amenities, Highways, Health & Leisure for further exploration. Recommendations from the Communications Working Party. a) To Agree the draft Digital Screen Policy for Ramsey Town Council previously circulated. Proposed by Cllr L Knight and seconded by Cllr S Corney Ramsey Town Council voted 10 FOR and 1 ABSTENTION to APPROVE the Digital Screen Policy. a) To Agree the Risk Assessment for Public Meetings at Ramsey Town Council- previously circulated. Proposed by Cllr L Knight and seconded by Cllr S Corney. Ramsey Town Council voted 9 FOR and 2 ABSTENTIONS to APPROVE the Risk Assessment for Public Meetings. b) To Agree the Risk Assessment for Premises and Buildings- previously circulated. Proposed by Cllr L Knight and seconded by Cllr S Corney Ramsey Town Council vote 9 FOR and 2 ABSTENTIONS to APPROVE the Risk Assessment for Premises and Buildings. c) To Review the current IT Policy – previously circulated. Proposed by Cllr L Knight and seconded by Cllr S Corney Ramsey Town Council voted 10 FOR and 1 ABSTENTION to APPROVE the updated IT Policy. d) To agree the new email footer –tabled. Proposed by Cllr L Knight and seconded by Cllr S Corney Ramsey Town Council vote 10 FOR and 1 ABSTENTION to use the footer tabled for Councillor emails. The Clerk will circulate to members to use. 284. WORKING PARTY UPDATE a) Members to receive an update from the Chair of each Working Party- previously circulated. Cllr L Knight said this was a very useful document and is a really good idea. The document was noted.
285. FEEDBACK FROM GRANT FROM COMMUNITY SAFETY & SAFETY PARTNERSHIP.

a) Feedback from Future Scooter Foundation -the Clerk showed two small video clips from some of the young people who participated in the evening event. There was a positive debate, and it was agreed that it would be good to have more young girls participating. Noted

286. TOWN MAYOR’S AND CLERK’S CORRESPONDENCE: a) Update on Anti-Social Behaviour on the Clerk and Council. The Clerk updated members on the investigation with Huntingdonshire District Council Anti-Social behaviour team. They are now looking to produce a Criminal Behaviour Order to protect the Council. b) Resident communication on noise from skate park and concerns RTC would put lighting there for after dark use. The Clerk informed members that a resident after reading a District Councillors post on having lighting at the Skatepark was very upset as Ramsey Town Council had said that would not be the case. Cllr Fendley was very clear that there would be no plans to light up the Skatepark. c) Resident communication on thanking the Town Council for the work Paul and Morgan are doing keeping the Cemetery clear and improving the area. The Clerk informed members that positive comments had been received about the work in clearing the Cemetery. d) Thank you from the Ramsey Garden and Horticulture Club for the grant we gave them which enable two new competitions this year. Cllr Fendley informed members of the letter received thanking Ramsey Town Council for their grant and the opportunities it has given their club. e) Ramsey Heights residents concern over lack of Fire Hydrant for the Droves. After the fire on Harpers Drove, residents were concerned that the Fire Service had to keep going away to refill the tanker. This was noted. Councillor Costello left the meeting at 8:55pm. 287. ATTENDANCES AT MEETINGS AND ORGANISATIONS: a) Safer Communities Public Meeting - Cllr V Fendley fed back on the public meeting held at Ramsey Forty Foot. Cllr V Fendley praised the Inspector for his honesty during the meeting, but the overall outcome was we do live in a safe community. b) Mayor met with County Councillor Cllr H Tobias. Cllr V Fendley informed members that she had had a meeting and discussed the LHI bids and infrastructure. c) Magnolia Park Opening Day- Cllr V Fendley attended the opening and it was a very positive day. d) Jones Court 40 th Anniversary BBQ – Cllr V Fendley and the Clerk attended the BBQ, and Cllr V Fendley had the difficult task of judging the baking competition. e) Update on correspondence with Cambridgeshire Constabulary – Cllr R Terrill updated members on his conversation with Inspector Norden. f) MP Sam Carling – Local Surgery Date 14 th August 2026. Cllr V Fendley informed members that the MP was in the community meeting with residents.
288. MEETING DATES The next meeting of Ramsey Town Council (Planning) will take place on 27th August 2026 at 7pm.

governance.title: Co-option of New Town Councillor
governance.summary: Following presentations from three candidates, Jessie Thompson received the most votes and was co-opted to join the Town Council starting at the August planning meeting.

governance.title: Planning Applications Recommendations
governance.summary: The council voted unanimously to recommend approval for a damp proof course at Bridge Farm (Ramsey Road, Ramsey Forty Foot) and replacement cladding at 17 Wyatt Close (Ramsey). The council also voted to refuse a planning application for a gypsy and traveller residential pitch at Land East of Fern Cottage (Harpers Drove, Ramsey Heights) following resident objections.

governance.title: Appointment of Planning Consultant for Local Plan Consultation
governance.summary: The council voted (10 for, 1 against) to instruct Anthony Northcote to provide advice regarding Ramsey Town Council's response to the Huntingdonshire District Council Local Plan Consultation.

RAMSEY TOWN COUNCIL 
 
You are hereby summoned to attend a meeting of Ramsey Town Council to be held in The Lavender Room, 
Ramsey Town Council Great Whyte, Ramsey on Thursday 24 September 2026 at 7.00pm, when the 
following items of business will be transacted: - 
 
 
Please ensure all mobile phones are switched off or turned to silent during the meeting. 
 
A G E N D A  
   APOLOGIES FOR ABSENCE 
 
1. DECLARATIONS OF INTEREST 
To receive declarations from Members as to disclosable pecuniary and other interests and the nature of 
those interests in relation to any agenda item. 
   
2. PUBLIC PARTICIPATION 
To allow 20 minutes for any members of the public to address the Council.  
 
3. MINUTES 
To approve as a correct record, the Minutes of the meeting of the Council held on 10th September 2026 
– attached. 
 
4. PLANNING 
1.1 25/01382/OUT Outline application with all matters reserved save for access for erection of up to 199 
dwellings including open space, play space, car parking, drainage, utilities connections and the 
construction of a new access off Stoneman Way and Biggin Lane – further information received. 
1.2 26/00681/FUL Construction of 2 drive-thru units (sui generis) with associated hard and soft 
landscaping – Plot 09A St Marys Road, Ramsey. 
1.3 26/01584/FUL Open storage of vehicles (Use Class B8) in association with the adjacent vehicle 
scrapping, recycling and export businesses – Land South of The Foundry, Factory Bank, Ramsey. 
1.4 26/01670/S73 Variation of condition 2 (Approved Plans – Planning Applications) of 25/02222/FUL – 
Land Rear of 192 Oilmills Road, Ramsey Mereside. 
 
  Planning Other Business 
a) Somersham Neighbourhood Plan Consultation 
       Ramsey Town Council comments to be agreed. 
b) Street Naming: Equestrian Facilities, Land on south side of Middle Drove, Ramsey Heights to be 
known as The Meadows, Middle Drove, Ramsey Heights. 
c) Huntingdonshire Pre Submission Local Plan – 2046, Ramsey Town Council response – Email 
received regarding Site Allocation Bury 1 (Old Station Road, Bury development) – previously 
circulated. 
d) Mews Car Park and Great Whyte Improvements Update 
 
5. RESIDENTS COMMUNICATION  
To be noted - tabled 
 
 
Would Cllrs please make time to look at the planning items on the District Council’s website 
before the meeting by accessing the HDC planning portal.  
  
  
6. MEETING DATES 
The next meeting of Ramsey Town Council will take place at 7pm on 8th October 2026.  
 
 
 Lisa Renfree                     18th September 2026 
     
      Town Clerk 
 
 

 
 
 
MINUTES OF RAMSEY TOWN COUNCIL MEETING 
held at 7pm on Thursday 10 September 2026 at  
Ramsey Town Council Great Whyte, Ramsey 
 
 
Present:  Councillors: A Austin, I Axelsen, J Bufton, J Clarke, M Clarke, S Corney, A Costello, V Fendley (Mayor), S Fice, 
L Knight, R Terrill, J Thompson, and L Webster. 
In attendance: Mrs L Renfree, Town Clerk  
 
297. Apologies for Absence. 
Cllrs J Aubin, C Maskell, P Rose and E Welsh. 
 
298.To Receive Declarations of Interest. 
No declarations of interest were made. 
 
299. Public Participation. 
There  was  one  member  of  the  public  who  wished  to  speak  and  encouraged  the  Town  Council  to  continue  to  use  Future 
Scooters for young person training for the skate park. 
 
300. Minutes of the Last Meeting to be Approved. 
Councillors voted unanimously to accept the Minutes of the meeting of the Council held on 27
th
 August 2026 as a correct 
record. 
 
301. District Councillor & County Councillor Updates: 
Cllrs H Tobias, and R Coogan attended the meeting, and no apologies were received from Cllr K Maheshwari. Cllr Tobias 
informed the members that he would be looking at the roads in the area with the Senior Officer for Highways and would be 
attending his first County Council meeting on 13
th
 October. 
Cllr Coogan informed members that the Local Government Reorganisation has been paused. Cllr Coogan informed 
members that he abstained from the Local Plan knowing it would be approved, his party wouldn’t allow them to vote for it 
but he knew our Council wanted it to go through. With the Local Plan going through it would mean the area should get 
more infrastructure. Cllr A Austin asked Cllr Coogan to investigate why the Town Council’s application for strategic CIL 
could not be applied for, for play parks. Cllr S Corney asked Cllr Coogan to investigate why there was a hold on the 
decision on the land at Mews Close due to the parking strategy, as it currently is waste land not a car park. 
 Council noted that there had been no mention of provision in the Local Plan for Traveller and Gypsy sites.  
 
302. Planning Applications for Consideration. 
1.1 26/01440/FUL Change of use to a SEN day school (Class F1), erection of a rear single storey extension, external 
alterations to existing two-storey rear extension and associated works including additional car parking, new landscaping and 
recreation areas – Westward House, Bury Road, Ramsey. Proposed by Cllr L Knight and seconded by Cllr S Fice Ramsey 
Town Council voted UNANIMOUSLY for the District Council to APPROVE the application. There were no neighbouring 
objections. Members did note the County Council concerns on the size of the in and out areas, but members felt this could 
easily be mitigated. 
 
1.2 26/01089/HHFUL Proposed replacement roof to form first floor accommodation, demolition of the existing porch and 
erection of a new single storey porch, erection of a new balcony, installation of external insulation and cladding to the 
existing dwelling and associated internal alterations – Living Accommodation Stokes Garage, Ramsey Road, Ramsey Forty 
Foot. Proposed by Cllr A Costello and seconded by Cllr M Clarke, Ramsey Town council voted UNANNIMOUSLY for the 
District Council to APPROVE the application. There were no neighbouring objections. 
 
 
303. Planning – other business 
a) Local Plan 2046 – Cllr V Fendley informed members that Huntingdonshire District Council’s Local 
Plan had been approved and it goes to final consultation from 16
th
 September 2026 and ends 28
th
 
October 2026. As previously been mentioned having a local plan shows an intent to develop and 
supports getting infrastructure. Previously Ramsey Town Council had voted to use the Planning 
Consultant to support the response from Ramsey Town Council. There would be comment about 
the lack of provision for Traveller/Gypsy sites and would also include what would be in the Ramsey 
Communities Neighbourhood Plan for the site at Stoneman Way proposed by David Wilson Homes.  
b) Neighbourhood Plan Independent Inspector Report Update. Cllr V Fendley informed members that 
the Independent Assessor had read the plan and supported the view of no further coalition with 
Bury Parish. It is proposed that the community referendum would take place in December. 
  
304. FINANCE ITEMS 
a) Financial Summary - Cash book to 31/8/26 - Noted 

b) Expenditure Transactions to be approved– Proposed by Cllr L Knight and seconded by Cllr S Corney 
Ramsey Town Council voted UNANIMOUSLY to APPROVE the expenditure transactions. 
c) To approve the implementation of the Local Government, Pay Award - Pay rates and allowances have been 
increased by 3.3% with effect from 1
st
 April 2026. Proposed by Cllr S Fice and seconded by Cllr L Knight 
Ramsey Town Council voted UNANIMOUSLY to APPROVE the pay award. 
d) Updated Grant Form – Cllr A Austin presented the new guidance on the grant forms and the scoring system. 
Cllr A Austin explained the three tiers which would cover the small, medium, and large grant applications. 
Proposed by Cllr A Austin and seconded by Cllr L Webster, Ramsey Town Council voted UNANIMOUSLY to 
APPROVE the grant application form and matrix. 
 
305. Future Scooter Permission 
Future Scooters had asked Ramsey Town Council if they could hold one to one training sessions on the QEII 
Skate Park. Proposed by Cllr S Fice and seconded by Cllr L Webster Rasmey Town Council voted 
UNANIMOUSLY to APPROVE Future Scooters holding one-to one sessions at the Skate Park but the skate park 
would still be in use for other residents. 
 
306. Working Party Updates: 
Members had received an update from the Chair of each Working Party- noted 
 
307. Communications Working Party Recommendation: 
a) Draft newsletter – Cllr A Austin explained that the draft would be circulated once finalised. 
 
308. Town Mayor’s and Clerk’s Correspondence: 
a) Just Giving Fire Fighter Fund Update – Cllr V Fendley informed members that the final amount 
from the Just giving after they had taken their percentage was £4546.55- once all payments had 
been made there was a surplus of £1973.69  
At this point Cllr Coogan HDC District Councillor indicated he wished to speak. Cllr V Fendley 
suspended standing orders proposed by S Corney and seconded by Cllr J Bufton and Ramsey 
Town Council voted UNANIMOUSLY to suspend standing orders to allow Cllr Coogan to speak. 
Cllr Coogan informed members that he would be meeting with National Emergency Fund to 
support residents and businesses. Proposed by Cllr S Corney and seconded by Cllr J Bufton to 
bring back standing orders, Ramsey Town Council voted UNANIMOUSLY to put the Standing 
Orders back in place. 
Cllr S Corney proposed that the remaining funds were donated to the fire fighters Charity as described on 
the Just giving, Cllr A Austin put in a counter proposal to go back to Just Giving and ask the doners to 
decide on where it should go. This was seconded by Cllr M Clarke. Ramsey Town Council voted 7 FOR 6 
AGAINST 1 ABSTENTION, this then became the substantive motion proposed by Cllr A Austin and 
seconded by Cllr M Clarke Ramsey Town Council voted 8 FOR, 2 AGAINST and 3 ABSTENTIONS for the 
Just giving doners to be asked who they want the remaining funds to be donated to. 
b) FOI Response on CIL Funding Update- Cllr V Fendley informed members that the Freedom of 
Information request by Cllr K Maheshwari had been responded to, within two hours of the 
response being sent then Cllr K Maheshwari had put a post on Facebook with all the information 
given. A further Freedom of Information request then came in from Cllr K Maheshwari who asked 
for more information on the council’s decision making. Council noted the request. 
c) Emergency Planning Meeting – 1
st
 October 6:30pm at Ramsey Community Centre. Cllr V 
Fendley reminded members of the Emergency Planning Meeting. 
d) Climate Emergency Briefing- 23
rd
 September at St Thomas a Becket Church 6pm. Cllr V 
Fendley informed members of the Climate Emergency Briefing. 
e) Council to decide on centralised headstones in the lawn cemetery- After a discussion the 
Clerk was asked to take the matter back to the Cemetery Working Party. 
 
309.Attendances at Meetings and Organisations: 
a) Cllr V Fendley and Cllr S Corney attended the1940 Drumhead Service 
b) Heritage Day – Councillor Support. Cllr V Fendley thanked the Councillors for the support they 
would be giving at the Mortuary Chapel on Heritage Day. 
 
      310. District Wide Dog PSPO Renewal – Consultation- proposed by Cllr S Corney and seconded by Cllr R 
Terrill, Ramsey town Council voted UNANIMOUSLY to APPROVE the renewal of the District Wide Dog PSPO. 
 
311. Meeting Dates 
The next meeting of Ramsey Town Council would take place on Thursday 24th September at 7pm.

news.title: Ramsey Town Council Discusses Local Plan and Infrastructure
news.summary: During the September 10 meeting, councillors discussed local plan updates, roads, and upcoming planning considerations.
news.content: At the Ramsey Town Council meeting on 10 September 2026, county and district councillors provided updates regarding local roads, the paused Local Government Reorganisation, and the Local Plan 2046. Discussions also covered strategic CIL funding for play parks, the land at Mews Close parking strategy, and the absence of provisions for Traveller and Gypsy sites in the Local Plan.

governance.title: Planning Application Approvals and Reviews
governance.summary: The Council voted unanimously to recommend approval for planning application 26/01440/FUL (change of use to a SEN day school at Westward House, Bury Road) and 26/01089/HHFUL (replacement roof and alterations at Stokes Garage, Ramsey Road, Ramsey Forty Foot).

governance.title: Upcoming Planning Consultations and Street Naming
governance.summary: The council agenda includes reviewing major planning applications such as 199 dwellings off Stoneman Way and Biggin Lane, drive-thru units on St Marys Road, street naming for Equestrian Facilities at Middle Drove (Ramsey Heights) to 'The Meadows', and the Huntingdonshire Pre Submission Local Plan – 2046 response.

Autumn
2026
Ramsey Town Council
Residents Communication
RAMSEY COMMUNITIES NEIGHBOURHOOD PLAN
A further step forward
The Ramsey Communities Neighbourhood Plan has been prepared with local voices at the heart. People
gave their opinions via consultation over the summer of 2025 and the plan was then put together by a
steering group of residents before going back out as a draft for further consultation. We’re pleased to say
that it has also passed another significant step - Independent Assessment.
Further details can be found on the Ramsey Town Council website.
What happens next?
The next major step will be a community vote
through a referendum organised by
Huntingdonshire District Council, likely to be in
December 2026. It will be organised in the same
way as an election and everyone on the electoral
register will be notified. You will be asked whether
you accept the Neighbourhood Plan - yes or no.
We will produce a quick reference guide for anyone
who may not have time to read the full document.
Key points include:
Providing new infrastructure, facilities and
services so new development benefits existing,
new and future residents.
Supporting a vibrant community with places to
live, work, stay and play, including affordable
housing and housing with a local connection.
Protecting the historic environment, heritage
assets and green spaces that matter to the
community.
Having our Neighbourhood Plan in place will mean Ramsey
receives 25% of developer contributions rather than the
current 15%.
That means more money can be spent directly in our
community.
neighbourhood.plan@ramseytowncouncil.gov.uk

CIL - Community Infrastructure Levy
What is CIL? Community Infrastructure Levy, commonly referred to as CIL, is money collected by
Huntingdonshire District Council from certain new developments. The funding is then used to help
provide or improve infrastructure needed as communities grow.
The money collected is broadly divided into three areas:
Up to 5% can be retained by Huntingdonshire District Council towards the administration and
collection of CIL.
15% is normally allocated to the Town or Parish Council for the area where the development takes
place. Once an adopted Neighbourhood Plan is in place, this increases to 25%.
Most of the remaining funding is retained by Huntingdonshire District Council for larger strategic
infrastructure projects across the district.
Ramsey Town Council currently receives the 15% neighbourhood portion. Once the Ramsey
Communities Neighbourhood Plan is adopted, this will increase to 25%, giving the Council a greater
share of money from qualifying development to invest back into our communities.
Current projects supported or earmarked through Ramsey Town Council’s CIL funding include:
Improvements at The Moorings.
Contributions towards Local Highways Improvement projects.
Improvements to Newtown Road Play Park.
Improvements to the public toilets.
New benches at the skate park.
CCTV at The Moorings and New Road.
The Double Yellow Lines project.
The Town Council is also considering future projects, including additional parking behind the doctor’s
surgery at Mews Close.
Local Highways Initiative Bid (LHI): what is an LHI?
The Local Highway Improvement programme allows local councils and community organisations to
apply to Cambridgeshire County Council for funding towards highway improvements. Projects can
include new or extended footpaths, traffic-calming measures, speed-reduction schemes, and other
changes designed to improve road and pedestrian safety.
Ramsey Town Council identifies potential projects and submits applications to Cambridgeshire County
Council. Applications are assessed by the County Council and, if successful, funding is awarded
towards the cost of the scheme. Under the current scheme, up to £25,000 can be awarded towards
more complex projects, with applicants expected to contribute at least 10% of the overall cost.
One recent LHI project was the extension of the footpath along Stocking Fen Road towards the
industrial estate, improving pedestrian access for people travelling to and from work. The Council has
also submitted an application for speed-reduction measures on the approach to Ramsey St Mary’s and
is awaiting the outcome.
Abbey College Road Safety Campaign
Abbey College students are raising funds towards the £10,000 needed to help
pay for speed reduction measures on Hollow Lane. Students have been
campaigning, the school submitted an LHI bid, and speed cushions are
planned. They would be grateful if you could spare the price of a coffee and
scan the QR code.

Message from the Mayor of Ramsey
Hello everyone, I hope you’ve all had a wonderful summer. Personally, I can’t
believe how quickly this year has flown by and that, as I write this, we’re already
going into autumn. 
I want to use this column to recognise some amazing people - the Ramsey
Town Council staff team, led by our Clerk, Lisa Renfree. They have had an
incredibly busy summer, with lots of change and new initiatives to contend with
as our Council grows and new Councillors come on board with the ambition to
achieve and deliver more for our residents.
They organised the Bands on the Green programme, delivered a family fun day at QEII Park with
entertainment from the Blues Brothers and Queen tribute acts, produced and managed delivery of our
newsletters to 5,000 homes, and got to grips with a new finance system. This was all on top of day-to-
day customer service and administration, room bookings, council meetings and communications. They
also stepped up to help coordinate meals and drinks for firefighters at Holme Fen during the recent
wildfire, when the RRT Charity had to leave after a week.
They do all of this professionally and with a smile. More often, however, they are facing abusive
behaviour and, as a Council, this is something we will not tolerate. We have had to notify the police
and use CCTV as evidence. Thankfully, this behaviour comes from a minority, and I know many of you
appreciate the time our staff takes to assist you. So, from me and all fellow Councillors: thank you Lisa,
Amanda, Kay, Alison, Quincy, Morgan and Paul - you are appreciated. Keep up the great work for our
community.
Thank you, Ramsey Parish community and beyond
On behalf of Ramsey Town Council, we would like to thank
everyone who supported the firefighters responding to the fire at
Holme Fen. The response from local businesses, organisations
and volunteers was incredible. Our thanks go to The Farmers
Coffee Shop, Gorilla Pizza and Friar Tuck Fish & Chips for
providing food and support; Ramsey Community Centre for
opening its kitchen to prepare the large quantity of meals needed;
The Admiral Wells for becoming a hub of activity, preparing meals
and acting as a donation drop-off point; and Stevelyn & Creative
Crafters for also providing a collection point, to name just a few.
We would also like to thank the many volunteers who gave their time to prepare food and help
wherever needed, as well as everyone who made donations. The JustGiving appeal raised an amazing
£4,546.56. The Mayor also had the privilege of meeting The Duke of Gloucester during his visit to
Holme Fen, where he saw the devastation caused by the fire and personally thanked firefighters, the
owners of The Admiral Wells and local volunteers for their incredible efforts.
The Lord-Lieutenant, Julie Spence, who accompanied him, spoke of how proud
she was to see the community come together so quickly and effectively.
Firefighters expressed their appreciation for every meal, drink and homemade
cake provided during the response.
Following the fire, a meeting of local community groups has been arranged for 1
October to discuss emergency planning and how the community can work
together in response to future major incidents.

Meet the new Town Council members
My husband and I chose Ramsey 26 years ago based on what we felt it had to
offer us as a family and our growing children: the wonderful people, the community,
the facilities, the coffee shops, the leisure centre and the parks. There have been
many changes since then, and I want to make sure Ramsey remains that
wonderful place. Hopefully, my role as a magistrate, my previous experience with
numerous community groups and the experience of raising my children in this
community will stand me in good stead to help the people of Ramsey further.
If you have opinions about the community in which you live, then for me, it is
important to express them in a positive way by becoming involved in the decision-
making forums and involving yourself actively and practically in the implementation
of ideas. In addition, having benefited from living in Ramsey for many years, I also
felt that it was time to repay some of those benefits by contributing, in some small
part, to the development of our community. I therefore took a leap of faith earlier
this year and put my name forward for election to the town council.
 
My family and I moved to Ramsey two years ago, and what began as a new
chapter has become home. With my daughter attending school locally, I have seen
how important a connected, inclusive community is. I want her to grow up
somewhere people feel proud to call home. Throughout my career, including my
recent role in strategic transformation and programme management at M&S, I have
developed strong skills in collaboration, listening and turning ideas into action. I
want to bring these values to Ramsey, listening to residents and supporting our
town’s continued growth. Please say hello and share your thoughts when you see
me around town. 
Freedom of the Town – Pat Taylor
Freedom of the Town is the highest honour a Town Council can
award. On Sunday 20th September 2026, it was awarded to Pat
Taylor for her commitment to Ramsey.
Pat was an English teacher for many years and has taught lots of
residents; however, her volunteering means that she is also
known in many other capacities, spread across the years.
She was a Trustee of Ramsey Welfare Charities and Jones
Court, supporting our older residents; she volunteered at the
foodbank, where Reverend Richard Darmody said her help and
support were invaluable.
Council meeting dates - All residents are welcome
Ramsey Town Council meets on the second Thursday of every month at 7 pm in the Council Building
on Great Whyte. Residents are welcome to listen and have an opportunity at the start of the meeting to
address Council members.
8 October · 12 November · 10 December · 14 January · 11 February · 11 March
8 April · 13 May (AGM) · 10 June · 8 July · 12 August · 9 September
Pat was part of the steering committee that helped to form Ramsey U3A, and she was the first Chair
from 2011 to 2012, remaining a member to the present day.
She has also been a Town Councillor, serving for 26 years until her recent retirement, and has been
Mayor of Ramsey twice.
Her nomination for the Freedom of Ramsey was put forward by Cllr Adela Costello and was
wholeheartedly approved by fellow Councillors. Our congratulations to Pat; thank you for all you have
done to support our community.
Cllr Webster
Cllr Axelsen
Cllr Thompson

Public Toilets - New Road
The Moorings
It has been lovely to see residents and young people making use of
the improvements at The Moorings, including young people fishing
and spending time with friends.
Ramsey Town Council is also working with Ramsey Rotary to
introduce crocuses and other planting to bring more colour to the
area. The improvements at The Moorings have been funded through
the Community Infrastructure Levy (CIL). 
Ramsey Town Council is currently replacing the doors at the public toilets and has installed a payment
facility, which will come into operation once the refurbishment works are complete. The Council has
decided to introduce a small charge for use of the facilities to reduce anti-social behaviour and help
ensure the toilets remain clean and in good condition. CCTV will also be installed on New Road to help
identify those responsible for anti-social behaviour and to support Huntingdonshire District Council and
the police in dealing with incidents.
Skate Park Benches and No to Floodlights
As we go to print, the Council is selecting and arranging new picnic benches to be installed near the
skate park, ready for spring 2027. These, together with the new concrete rumble-strip area, are
expected to be in place in October and some grass seeding will continue to improve the area for young
people and residents.
There has recently been incorrect information circulating on social media suggesting that the Council is
considering floodlighting at the skate park. This is not the case. When the Council agreed to the skate
park, it was clear that the facility should not be encouraged for use after dark. This also reflects
feedback from nearby residents who have contacted the Clerk and Councillors with concerns about the
potential for increased anti-social behaviour during the evening.
Newtown Road Under-5s Play Park Improvement
Residents will have seen that the new fencing to extend the under-5s play area has now been
completed. The public consultation has also been launched and shared with residents and nurseries
across the Ramsey area. Ramsey Town Council has listened to feedback from families with young
children about the limited amount of play equipment currently available and the need to update the
existing facilities.
With a growing number of young families in the area, the Council felt it was important to make
Newtown Road Play Park a priority, particularly as other play parks across the town have benefited
from new equipment over the last three years.

Bands on the Green 2026
Bands on the Green has been really successful. The
weather was very kind to us - sometimes almost too hot!
It was good to have some new bands join us this year,
including the Abbey College Band and Janine Mitchell
singing. Ramsey Town Council would like to thank the
team of volunteers at St Thomas a Becket Church for
supplying teas, coffee and scrumptious cake.
Heritage Day - Sunday 13 September
Heritage Day was very popular this year, and it
was wonderful to meet people from as far away as
Berkshire and Essex. The Heritage Partnership
funded reenactments of the Vikings, the Sealed
Knot, and the Romans. Luckily, the Mayor
survived the stocks!
Heritage Day showcases our history: Ramsey Rural Museum, Victorian Walled Garden, Abbey
Gatehouse, St Thomas a Becket Church and the Mortuary Chapels.
The Hangout - Youth Club every Thursday
Ramsey Neighbourhoods Trust has launched its youth club, The
Hangout. It is open to all young people aged 11+ and is held at
the Pavilion on Cricketfield Lane. The youth club is open from
6.15pm to 7.45pm every Thursday during term time. Ramsey
Town Council is pleased to fund the youth club.
Youth Café has opened again and runs every Monday from
3.30pm to 6pm at The Farmers Café. It is free to attend, tuck is
available, and it provides a safe place to hang out with friends.
BOSH is the club for younger people. It is held every Thursday during term time from 4.30pm to 6pm,
offering children fun and games.

Rotary in Ramsey
Anti-Social Behaviour - How to Report
Ramsey Town Council has recently received several requests for CCTV cameras in different areas of
the community following concerns about anti-social behaviour.
Reports of anti-social behaviour should be made to Huntingdonshire District Council. Reporting
incidents is important because it helps build an accurate picture of where problems are occurring and
provides the evidence needed for the relevant authorities to take action.
Anti-social behaviour can be reported online at:
forms.huntingdonshire.gov.uk/REPORTANTISOCIALBEHAVIOUR/launch
Alternatively, email communityaction@huntingdonshire.gov.uk or call 01480 388388.
One-to-one meeting with a Councillor
If you would like to speak to a Councillor on a one-to-one basis about a local
issue, concern, or idea, appointments can be arranged throughout the week,
including evenings and weekends.
This allows residents to discuss matters directly with a Councillor at a time
that is convenient for them.
Simply scan the QR code, complete the short form and request an
appointment. A suitable time can then be arranged with you.
Ramsey Business Forum
Ramsey Town Council is launching its first Business Forum on Tuesday 13 October at 6pm at The
George, Ramsey. 
The forum will give local businesses a direct opportunity to raise concerns, share ideas, and help
shape the Council’s new Economic Development work, focused on increasing footfall and supporting
local businesses.
All Businesses are welcome.
Ramsey Town Council is pleased to continue its close
relationship with Rotary in Ramsey. The Clerk and Rotary’s
Secretary regularly meet to share information and work
together on events.
The Council looks forward to hosting one of the Santa Float evenings
for the volunteers after they have been out raising funds.
To get involved, contact
secretary@ramseyrotary.co.uk and book to
attend the planning evening on Wednesday 11
November.
Look out for the Santa Tracker to find
out when he will visit your street.

Raising funds for the Mayor’s
charities: Ramsey Rural Museum and
the Armed Services Veterans
Breakfast Club.
No experience is needed - trust the
process and you will have loads of fun
and create a wonderful item.
Click the QR code to book or email
events@ramseytowncouncil.gov.uk
.
Events for you to come along and enjoy
Scan the QR code
to donate. Every
pound is very much
appreciated.
Ramsey Christmas Lights is putting the
tree up on Saturday 14 November.
Complete the festive trail to collect your
bauble, decorate it and have it hung on the
tree. That afternoon there will be a children’s
Christmas Party, a chance to have a family
photograph taken by a professional
photographer, Santa in his grotto for a selfie
and a Snow Globe. The party is free and will
be held at Ramsey Community Centre, with
refreshments on sale.
Switch-On Day - Saturday 28 November. The morning
starts at 10am at Abbey College with the Christmas
Bazaar. The town-centre switch-on starts at 3pm with a
Taylor Swift tribute, and the lights go on at 5.15pm. The
fairground will be in town until 8pm. There is an envelope
with this newsletter, or you can scan the QR code above.
Festive Markets
Saturday 5 December
Saturday 12 December
Saturday 19 December
To book a stall, contact:
events@ramseytowncouncil.gov.uk
Festive Extravaganza
Saturday 12 December, 9am-1pm
Come and join Santa, make a free gift and see
who might visit!

Youth Café has opened again and runs every Monday from 3.30pm to 6pm at The Farmers Café. It is free to attend, tuck is available, and it provides a safe place to hang out with friends. BOSH is the club for younger people. It is held every Thursday during term time from 4.30pm to 6pm, offering children fun and games.

Rotary in Ramsey Anti-Social Behaviour - How to Report Ramsey Town Council has recently received several requests for CCTV cameras in different areas of the community following concerns about anti-social behaviour. Reports of anti-social behaviour should be made to Huntingdonshire District Council. Reporting incidents is important because it helps build an accurate picture of where problems are occurring and provides the evidence needed for the relevant authorities to take action. Anti-social behaviour can be reported online at: forms.huntingdonshire.gov.uk/REPORTANTISOCIALBEHAVIOUR/launch Alternatively, email communityaction@huntingdonshire.gov.uk or call 01480 388388. One-to-one meeting with a Councillor If you would like to speak to a Councillor on a one-to-one basis about a local issue, concern, or idea, appointments can be arranged throughout the week, including evenings and weekends. This allows residents to discuss matters directly with a Councillor at a time that is convenient for them. Simply scan the QR code, complete the short form and request an appointment. A suitable time can then be arranged with you. Ramsey Business Forum Ramsey Town Council is launching its first Business Forum on Tuesday 13 October at 6pm at The George, Ramsey. The forum will give local businesses a direct opportunity to raise concerns, share ideas, and help shape the Council’s new Economic Development work, focused on increasing footfall and supporting local businesses. All Businesses are welcome. Ramsey Town Council is pleased to continue its close relationship with Rotary in Ramsey. The Clerk and Rotary’s Secretary regularly meet to share information and work together on events. The Council looks forward to hosting one of the Santa Float evenings for the volunteers after they have been out raising funds. To get involved, contact secretary@ramseyrotary.co.uk and book to attend the planning evening on Wednesday 11 November. Look out for the Santa Tracker to find out when he will visit your street.

Raising funds for the Mayor’s charities: Ramsey Rural Museum and the Armed Services Veterans Breakfast Club. No experience is needed - trust the process and you will have loads of fun and create a wonderful item. Click the QR code to book or email events@ramseytowncouncil.gov.uk . Events for you to come along and enjoy Scan the QR code to donate. Every pound is very much appreciated. Ramsey Christmas Lights is putting the tree up on Saturday 14 November. Complete the festive trail to collect your bauble, decorate it and have it hung on the tree. That afternoon there will be a children’s Christmas Party, a chance to have a family photograph taken by a professional photographer, Santa in his grotto for a selfie and a Snow Globe. The party is free and will be held at Ramsey Community Centre, with refreshments on sale. Switch-On Day - Saturday 28 November. The morning starts at 10am at Abbey College with the Christmas Bazaar. The town-centre switch-on starts at 3pm with a Taylor Swift tribute, and the lights go on at 5.15pm. The fairground will be in town until 8pm. There is an envelope with this newsletter, or you can scan the QR code above. Festive Markets Saturday 5 December Saturday 12 December Saturday 19 December To book a stall, contact: events@ramseytowncouncil.gov.uk Festive Extravaganza Saturday 12 December, 9am-1pm Come and join Santa, make a free gift and see who might visit!

news.title: Ramsey Communities Neighbourhood Plan Advances to Referendum
news.summary: The Ramsey Communities Neighbourhood Plan has passed independent assessment and is heading toward a community referendum in December 2026.
news.content: The Ramsey Communities Neighbourhood Plan, prepared following consultations starting in the summer of 2025, has successfully passed Independent Assessment. The next major step will be a community referendum organized by Huntingdonshire District Council, expected in December 2026, where residents on the electoral register will vote on whether to accept the plan. Adoption of the plan will increase Ramsey's share of developer contributions (CIL) from 15% to 25%, providing more funding to be spent directly in the community.

news.title: Abbey College Students Launch Road Safety Campaign for Hollow Lane
news.summary: Students at Abbey College are fundraising to help pay for speed reduction measures, including planned speed cushions, on Hollow Lane.
news.content: Abbey College students are actively campaigning and raising funds toward the £10,000 required to help pay for speed reduction measures on Hollow Lane. The school previously submitted a Local Highways Improvement (LHI) bid, and speed cushions are planned to improve pedestrian and road safety.

governance.title: Ramsey Communities Neighbourhood Plan Referendum Scheduled
governance.meetingTitle: Ramsey Town Council / Huntingdonshire District Council
governance.summary: The Neighbourhood Plan has passed independent assessment and will proceed to a public referendum organized by Huntingdonshire District Council in December 2026.

governance.title: Update on CIL Funded Projects and Future Infrastructure Plans
governance.summary: Ramsey Town Council highlighted ongoing and completed Community Infrastructure Levy (CIL) projects, including improvements at The Moorings, Newtown Road Play Park, public toilets, skate park benches, CCTV installations, and a double yellow lines project. The council is also considering future parking provision behind the doctor's surgery at Mews Close.

governance.title: Local Highways Improvement (LHI) Updates and Applications
governance.meetingTitle: Ramsey Town Council / Cambridgeshire County Council
governance.summary: The council noted the recent completion of the Stocking Fen Road footpath extension toward the industrial estate and confirmed a new LHI application has been submitted seeking speed-reduction measures on the approach to Ramsey St Mary’s.

held at 7pm on Thursday 24 September 2026 at  
Ramsey Town Council Great Whyte, Ramsey 
 
 
Present:    Councillors: A Austin, I Axelsen, J Clarke, M Clarke, V Fendley (Mayor), S Fice, 
L Knight, P Rose, R Terrill, J Thompson, and L Webster. 
In attendance: Mrs L Renfree, Town Clerk  
 
312. Apologies for Absence. 
Cllrs J Bufton, S Corney (representing the Council at RAF Wyton) A Costello, C Maskell, and 
E Welsh. 
 
313.To Receive Declarations of Interest. 
No declarations of interest were made. 
 
314. Public Participation. 
There was one member of the public who wished to thank the Town Council for awarding her 
the Freedom of the Town. 
 
315. Minutes of the Last Meeting to be Approved. 
Proposed by Cllr A Austin and seconded by Cllr R Terrill, Councillors voted unanimously to 
accept the Minutes of the meeting of the Council held on 10
th
 September 2026 as a correct 
record. 
 
316. Planning Applications for Consideration. 
1.1 25/01382/OUT Outline application with all matters reserved save for access for erection 
of up to 199 dwellings including open space, play space, car parking, drainage, utilities 
connections and the construction of a new access off Stoneman Way and Biggin Lane – 
further information received. Proposed by Cllr S Fice and seconded by Cllr P Rose Ramsey 
Town Council members voted UNANIMOUSLY for the District Council to REFUSE the 
application. The traffic assessment had not been actioned on the correct miles per hour- it 
stated 30mph when it is 20mph road. It is in Bury Parish Council’s adopted Local Plan and in 
the Draft Local Plan for Ramsey that the land needs to remain undeveloped to stop further 
coalescence between Bury Village and Ramsey Town. Drainage remains a concern for 
members for the area of land not having enough drainage in place and water would then be 
flowing into Slade Dyke. 
 
1.2 26/00681/FUL Construction of 2 drive-thru units (sui generis) with associated hard and 
soft landscaping – Plot 09A St Marys Road, Ramsey. Proposed by Cllr P Rose and seconded 
by Cllr S Fice Ramsey Town Council voted UNANIMOUSLY for the District Council to 
APPROVE the application.  
 
1.3 26/01584/FUL Open storage of vehicles (Use Class B8) in association with the adjacent 
vehicle scrapping, recycling, and export businesses – Land South of The Foundry, Factory 
Bank, Ramsey. Proposed by Cllr L Knight and seconded by Cllr R Terrill Ramsey Town 
Council voted 11 FOR and 1 ABSTENTION for the Clerk to gain further information before a 
formal vote would be submitted. The questions to be asked were, has the land had change of 
use from agricultural land? Has the environmental work been looked at for contamination? 
Has the drainage been looked at? Concerns on the land encroaching the area that would be 
siting the MUGA on the Northern Gateway. 
 
 

1.4 26/01670/S73 Variation of condition 2 (Approved Plans – Planning Applications) of 
25/02222/FUL – Land Rear of 192 Oilmills Road, Ramsey Mereside. Proposed by Cllr S 
Fice and seconded by Cllr M Clarke Ramsey Town Council voted UNANIMOUSLY for the 
District Council to APPROVE the application. Council saw no reason to object to the 
variations being made 
317. Planning – other business 
a) Somersham Neighbourhood Plan Consultation Ramsey Town Council comments 
to be agreed. Ramsey Town Council comments were to wish them well with their 
Local Plan. 
b) Street Naming: Equestrian Facilities, Land on south side of Middle Drove, Ramsey 
Heights to be known as The Meadows, Middle Drove, Ramsey Heights. Noted 
 
c) Huntingdonshire Pre Submission Local Plan – 2046, Ramsey Town Council 
response – Email received regarding Site Allocation Bury 1 (Old Station Road, Bury 
development) – previously circulated. Proposed by Cllr S Fice and seconded by Cllr A 
Austin the members voted UNANIMOUSLY for the Clerk to forward the email to the 
Planning consultant to add into their response. 
 
d) Mews Car Park and Great Whyte Improvements Update – The Mayor Cllr V 
Fendley updated the members on the two meetings she had had with the Portfolio 
holder for Governance about the Pedestrianisation Project. They felt it was a positive 
project and could see the benefits it would bring to the town. The Portfolio Holder also 
felt the land at the back of the Doctors on Mews Close was required for parking and 
asked the District Council team to move forward with the agreement of a Town 
Council lease hold of 50 years. He encouraged the Mayor to apply for this round of 
the HDC CIL funding to enable the work. 
 
318. Residents Communication. 
a) Draft newsletter – Cllr A Austin tabled the newsletter which was authorised to go to 
print. 
 
319. Meeting Dates 
The next meeting of Ramsey Town Council would take place on Thursday 8th October at 
7pm.
