Concerns on the land encroaching the area that would be siting the MUGA on the Northern Gateway.

1.4 26/01670/S73 Variation of condition 2 (Approved Plans – Planning Applications) of 25/02222/FUL – Land Rear of 192 Oilmills Road, Ramsey Mereside. Proposed by Cllr S Fice and seconded by Cllr M Clarke Ramsey Town Council voted UNANIMOUSLY for the District Council to APPROVE the application. Council saw no reason to object to the variations being made 317. Planning – other business a) Somersham Neighbourhood Plan Consultation Ramsey Town Council comments to be agreed. Ramsey Town Council comments were to wish them well with their Local Plan. b) Street Naming: Equestrian Facilities, Land on south side of Middle Drove, Ramsey Heights to be known as The Meadows, Middle Drove, Ramsey Heights. Noted

c) Huntingdonshire Pre Submission Local Plan – 2046, Ramsey Town Council response – Email received regarding Site Allocation Bury 1 (Old Station Road, Bury development) – previously circulated. Proposed by Cllr S Fice and seconded by Cllr A Austin the members voted UNANIMOUSLY for the Clerk to forward the email to the Planning consultant to add into their response.

d) Mews Car Park and Great Whyte Improvements Update – The Mayor Cllr V Fendley updated the members on the two meetings she had had with the Portfolio holder for Governance about the Pedestrianisation Project. They felt it was a positive project and could see the benefits it would bring to the town. The Portfolio Holder also felt the land at the back of the Doctors on Mews Close was required for parking and asked the District Council team to move forward with the agreement of a Town Council lease hold of 50 years. He encouraged the Mayor to apply for this round of the HDC CIL funding to enable the work.
318. Residents Communication. a) Draft newsletter – Cllr A Austin tabled the newsletter which was authorised to go to print.
319. Meeting Dates The next meeting of Ramsey Town Council would take place on Thursday 8th October at 7pm.

MINUTES OF RAMSEY TOWN COUNCIL MEETING 
held at 7pm on Thursday 08 October 2026 at  
Ramsey Town Council Great Whyte, Ramsey 
 
 
Present:    Councillors: A Austin, I Axelsen, J Bufton, J Clarke, M Clarke, Cllrs S Corney, V 
Fendley (Mayor), S Fice, L Knight, P Rose, R Terrill, J Thompson, L Webster and E Welsh. 
In attendance: Mrs L Renfree, Town Clerk  
 
320. Apologies for Absence. 
 Cllrs A Costello, C Maskell. 
 
321.To Receive Declarations of Interest. 
No declarations of interest were made at that point. 
 
322. Public Participation. 
There was six members of  the  public  who discussed  planning  1.3, discussing the potential 
199 David  Wilson  Homes  which was  going  to  be  debated  on  19
th
 October  at  Development 
Management Panel and a question was raised to be answered post that meeting on where 
the community would stand to make a legal challenge. 
 
323. Minutes of the Last Meeting to be Approved. 
Proposed by Cllr S Corney and seconded by Cllr L Knight, Councillors voted 13 FOR and 2 
ABSTENSIONS for the Minutes of the meeting of the Council held on 24
th
 September 2026 
as a correct record. 
 
324.County and District Councillor Update. 
County and District Councillor Cllr H Tobias attended the meeting to feedback on both County 
and District matters. Cllr Tobias outlined two visits to Ashbeach School and Abbey College 
and  commented  on  the  challenges  that  Ashbeach  faced  with  lack  of  SEN  funding  and 
commented on the brilliant discipline of the students in behaviour at Abbey College. As the 
County Councillor Cllr Tobias had been out with the Highways Officer to discuss the state of 
the roads in the community, and the biggest block is the funding to repair underneath the roads 
instead they are only able to fund patching them. Cllr Tobias then went on to discuss the 199 
David Wilson Homes and informed members that further housing would be coming at the RAF 
Upwood   site   and   still   with   no   infrastructure in   place.   Cllr   Tobias   touched   on   the 
Pedestrianisation and welcomed better communication on the project. Cllr Tobias was asked 
by the Mayor if he had any information on the pilot project on resurfacing the Fen Roads – Cllr 
Tobias  had  not.  Cllr  J  Clarke  asked  Cllr  Tobais  about  the  waste  of  resource  on  the  use  of 
traffic  lights  when  no  work  is taking place.  Cllr  Tobias  noted  the  comments.  Cllr  Tobias  did 
state you can read what he had been achieving in his two columns in the local newspaper. 
 
Presentation from Ramsey Neighbourhoods Trust 
Cllr I Axelsen and Cllr J Aubin declared a non-pecuniary interest on this item as Trustees of 
Ramsey Neighbourhoods Trust. 
 
Sam and Sarah from Ramsey Neighbourhoods Trust gave a presentation to members with an 
overview of the community group, what they do and what services they provide. Sarah talked 
through the young people’s projects which Ramsey Town Council funding had been covering. 
Cllr Axelsen who is also the Chair of Ramsey Neighbourhoods Trust had previously circulated 
the funding figures to members. The funding for the following year would be discussed at the 
following Finance Working Party and form part of the 20278/28 budget. 
 
 

2 
 
325. Planning Applications for Consideration: 
 
1.1 3226/01526/FUL Temporary permission for a period of 15 years for the erection of 3 units 
for use as retail or community space and associated public realm and highway 
improvements – Pedestrian Island, Great Whyte, Ramsey. Proposed by Cllr S Corney and 
seconded by Cllr E Welsh Cllr S Corney proposed acceptance of the application. 
Proposed by Cllr A  Austin and seconded by Cllr M Clarke an amendment to Cllr s 
Corney’s proposal ‘There is insufficient information for Ramsey Town Council to be able to 
support the application.’ A vote was taken on the amendment 5 FOR, 3 AGAINST and 6 
ABSTENSIONS. This meant that the amendment became the substantive motion. There 
was confusion for the councillors who voted to abstain as they thought they would then be 
able to vote on the original proposal by Cllr S Corney, this was not the case once the 
amendment had become the substantive motion. The meeting then moved on to planning 
application 1.2  
1.2 25/01301/FUL Erection of owner/site managers dwelling to serve existing caravan site.  
The retention of 14 existing touring caravan pitches, toilet and shower block and 3 holiday 
lodges along with the erection of two new timber holiday lodges and four new holiday 
pods – Riverside Lake and Leisure, Mereside Drove, Ramsey Mereside. Proposed by Cllr 
S Corney and seconded by Cllr P Rose Ramsey Town Council voted UNANIMOUSLY for 
the District Council to APPROVE the application. Members were clear their previous 
comments still stood. 
1.3 26/01763/FUL Erection of 3 detached dwellings, 3 detached double garages and 
associated works – Oak Cottage, Forty Foot Bank, Ramsey Forty Foot. Cllrs A Austin, P 
Rose and S Corney declared a non-pecuniary interest as they knew the applicant. 
Proposed by Cllr S Corney and seconded by Cllr J Bufton for District Council to 
APPROVE the application - Ramsey Town Council voted 6 FOR, 8 AGAINST and 1 
ABSTENTION The majority vote was for the application to be REFUSED. Members 
shared the concerns of the neighbouring residents in attendance. 
1.4 26/01763/FUL/26/01764/LBC Proposed conversion and extension of existing curtilage 
listed outbuilding into a separate, independently owned dwellinghouse – Bodsey House, 
Bodsey Toll Road, Ramsey. Proposed by Cllr L Knight and seconded by Cllr P Rose 
Ramsey Town Council voted UNANIMOUSLY for the District Council to APPROVE the 
application 
1.5 25/01433/FUL /26/00045/REFUSL Land Far West of Romany Cottage, Bucks Drove, 
Ramsey St Marys. Proposed self-build dwelling to be used as site manager’s house.  
Appeal against refusal. Cllr J Clarke declared a non-pecuniary as a neighbour to the 
applicant. Proposed by Cllr M Clarke and seconded Ramsey Town Council 13 FOR and 2 
ABSTENTIONS for the District Council to keep the REFUSAL in place. Their previous 
comments stood. 
 
326. Planning – other business 
a) Latest Planning Tracker – noted 
b) Planning online training- Members were reminded of the online planning training that 
would take place on zoom on 21
st
 October 2026. The Clerk was asked to circulate the 
invitation again. 
 
327. Finance Items 
a) Financial summary – Cash book to 30/09/2026 – noted 

3 
 
b) Expenditure Transactions to be approved. Proposed by Cllr S Corney and seconded by 
Cllr S Fice Ramsey Town Council voted UNANIMOUSLY for the expenditure transactions 
to be APPROVED. 
c) Grant applications – The Clerk informed members that 13 applications had been 
received and they would go to the next Finance Working Party and approved at the 
November Full Council meeting. 
d) Budget 2027/28 – Cllr S Fice informed members that the budget packs would be sent 
out in the following week. 
 
328.Working Party Updates 
 Members to receive an update from the Chairs of each Working Party – the Clerk 
apologised it had not gone out with the agenda papers but circulated that day. 
 
329. Working Party Recommendations 
 Economic Development – Members were informed that the SLA agreement for the 
Discover Huntingdonshire website. 
 Communications – Members were informed that the Newtown Road Play Park 
Consultation had been completed and the response was overwhelmingly positive. 
 
330.Town Mayor’s and Clerk’s Correspondence 
a) Civic Service Feedback – Cllr V Fendley fed back to members on how much people 
appreciated the Civic Service and its community spirit and that a lovely handwritten letter had 
been received by the High Sheriff of Cambridgeshire which would be in the office if any 
member wished to read it. 
b) Zebra Crossing Location, Abbey College Local Highways Initiative Bid – Members were 
informed by Cllr V Fendley that the wording on the consultation had been changed as 
Ramsey Town Council had not supported the zebra crossing due to the loss of parking 
spaces it would cause outside St Thomas a Becket Church. The Clerk was asked to forward 
the link to members. 
c) Local Highways Initiative Bid (Ramsey St Mary’s Buffer zones) update. The Clerk tabled 
the information received from Highways that the bid had not been successful. Further 
clarification had been asked for and it would go to the Amenities, Highways and Leisure 
Working Party. 
d) FOI Feedback – The Clerk informed members that the FOI had been responded to and no 
further communication had taken place. 
e) Newsletter Distribution – The Clerk informed members that the newsletter was being 
distributed and being well received. 
f) Development Management Committee – The Mayor informed members that the DMC 
meeting would take place on the 19
th
 October and members could attend in person, register 
to speak, or watch via zoom. Cllr S Corney would be representing the views at the meeting of 
Ramsey Town Council. 
g) Ramsey Communities Neighbourhood Plan – The Mayor informed members that the 
referendum for the NHP would take place on Thursday 26
th
 November 2026. 
 
331. Car Park Land Lease 
To discuss the Heads of Terms for the lease – the Clerk had previously circulated the Heads 
of Terms for comment. Cllr J Clarke asked if the Clerk could push for a longer lease than 50 
years. No other comments were asked to be sent back to HDC. Once the lease has gone 
through HDC Legal it will come to members for sign off. 
 
332. Attendances at Meetings and Organisations 
a) Flood Action Planning Meeting – Cllr J Thompson fed back to members about the meeting 
and that the flood action group should be community led, focussed, and tested. 

4 
 
b) Emergency Planning for the Future – Cllr V Fendley informed members that the meeting 
had 16 residents in attendance a very robust discussion had taken place. Cllr J Thompson 
had taken on the responsibility of outing the actions into the provided template. 
c) LVEP Conference – Cllr V Fendley explained the LVEP positioning starting at the bottom 
with Discover Ramsey, then Discover Huntingdonshire, Loval Visitor Economy Partnership 
and topped by Visit England. Cllr L Knight fed back to members about the Local Visitor 
Economy Forum Conference. It was a very positive meeting with a shout out to Ramsey for 
signing the Service Level Agreement for Discover Huntingdonshire. Both Cllr L K night and 
Cllr V Fendley both attended and sat on the table with Visit England. 
 
333. Meeting Dates 
The next meeting of Ramsey Town Council would take place on Thursday 22nd October 
(Planning) at 7pm.

metadata.title: Man fighting for life in hospital after robbery at jewellery store
metadata.contentSnippet: A man is fighting for his life in hospital after a robbery at Lala Jewellers in Peterborough.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Man fighting for life in hospital after robbery at jewellery store
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: A man is fighting for his life in hospital after a robbery at a jewellery shop in Cambridgeshire. Emergency services were called to Lala Jewellers, in Gladstone Street, Peterborough, at around 11.50am on Saturday (November 14). It follows reports six men entered the store, including two who were wearing white, traditional Pakistani clothing. Two employees behind the counter were assaulted and shelves were emptied, before the men fled in separate vehicles. One employee, a 50-year-old man, was seriously injured and rushed to hospital, where he remains in a life threatening condition. The other employee, a 30-year-old man, suffered minor injuries. Detective Inspector Tracy Sawyer said: "This is a very concerning incident which has left one man seriously injured and we are carrying out extensive enquiries to identify those responsible. "We would like to hear from anyone who was in the Gladstone Street area at around the time of the robbery and saw anything suspicious either before or after the incident. "We would also urge anyone with CCTV, doorbell or dashcam footage from the area which may have captured something relevant to please get in touch." Those with information should contact police online or via 101 quoting reference 35/88602/26. Information can also be reported anonymously to Crimestoppers on 0800 555111. Have you got a story you want to share? Get in touch at oliver.murphy@newsquest.co.uk

metadata.title: Aldi to cut vegetable prices to just 8p each for limited time before Christmas
metadata.contentSnippet: Aldi to cut vegetable prices to just 8p each for limited time before Christmas - here is exactly when

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Aldi to cut vegetable prices to just 8p each for limited time before Christmas
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: Aldi has confirmed that it will be reducing the price of some of its vegetables to just 8p before Christmas. The supermarket chain has reduced the price of its vegetables during the festive season in recent years, allowing customers to cut the cost of their Christmas dinner and this year the offer returns. All year round, the supermarket offers its Super Six fruit and vegetables at reduced prices, and now it’s time to start thinking about getting the festive vegetables ready. The promotion will be available in stores from December 19 until December 24 and includes the following vegetables: The six vegetables will be available to buy for 8p each during the promotion. Aldi will also be offering low-cost solutions for the rest of your Christmas dinner, including turkey, gravy, Yorkshire puddings and sage and onion stuffing mix at the same time. Based on the prices below, Aldi says customers can enjoy a Christmas dinner for £1.36 per person: The total dinner price is £10.85 and typically serves eight people, making it £1.36 per person. It’s worth noting that the sage and onion stuffing and Yorkshire pudding price reductions will be available from November 25. Aldi also says customers will pay a price depending on the weight of their turkey, and the price above is based on a Small Fresh British Turkey weighing 3kg. The news comes as Aldi shoppers can once again get their hands on Aldi’s iconic Kevin the Carrot toys. Shoppers can now buy Kevin the Carrot, Katie and a collection of festive characters. The supermarket brought back its much-loved plush toys to the middle aisle (and its latest Christmas advert) from November 12, with prices starting at £3.49. Cauli Dog, the adorable star of this year's Christmas advert, is available for £3.99 – but Aldi has introduced a limit of just two per customer because of expected demand. Recommended reading: The plush toy range also includes Kevin the Carrot and Katie, both priced at £3.99, alongside Jasper, Chantenay and Baby, giving fans the chance to collect the whole festive family. As the toys are Specialbuys in Aldi’s middle aisle, they’re available while stocks last. What are your non-negotiable ingredients on a Christmas dinner? Let us know in the comments below.

metadata.title: Microsoft issues important update for all users following global outage
metadata.contentSnippet: Microsoft has issued an update, telling its customers that it has now fully restored its services after the global outage that started on Thursday this week.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Microsoft issues important update for all users following global outage
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: Microsoft has fully restored services following a major global IT outage. The disruption affected police forces, the NHS, businesses, courts, and schools. The US-based company confirmed this morning (November 14) that services were fully restored for all remaining affected customers. In a statement on its Microsoft 365 status page, the company said: "We have completed our efforts to address the underlying issue of the incident and restored service to the remaining impacted customers and regions. We are deeply sorry for the disruption this incident has caused our customers and partners. We know the trust they place in our services and take that responsibility extremely seriously. We are seeing broad recovery and stability across our services. This was a technical issue not related to cyber or AI / agents. The incident was introduced by an issue during an earlier network capacity upgrade that surfaced following a recent network change. We have addressed the underlying issue and continue to restore service to remaining customers and regions. Given the scale of demand, we restored services gradually, validating stability at each stage. While this took longer, it helped ensure a stable restoration. We will provide a full post-incident report once our review is complete. — Microsoft (@Microsoft) November 13, 2026 "Further updates can be found at MO1550821 in the Microsoft 365 admin center." The outage, which began around 6pm GMT on Thursday, November 12, disrupted email, messaging, and other Microsoft 365 services. The UK Government and others worldwide were forced to activate contingency plans. Microsoft said on Friday the disruption was due to a "technical issue not related to cyber or AI agents." Baroness Lloyd of Effra, the UK Government’s cyber minister, said the problem mainly affected back-office functions. Baroness Lloyd said there had been "limited reports of impact on frontline service delivery" and the incident had been "inconvenient and disruptive". She confirmed she had spoken with Microsoft UK chief executive Darren Hardman about the outage. Monitoring website Downdetector first showed a spike in users reporting problems with Microsoft Teams in the UK at about 6.15pm on Thursday. It recorded a surge in complaints, with more than 130,000 users in the US reporting problems with Outlook at its peak on Thursday evening. Millions of its customers were unable to send and receive emails through Outlook, while Microsoft’s Copilot AI assistant, Teams and other Microsoft 365 services were also affected for many. Other AI chat platforms, including OpenAI’s ChatGPT and Anthropic’s Claude, were disrupted. Police forces in England and Wales said on Friday that they could not receive crime reports online. NHS England said staff had switched to "long-standing measures" to manage the outage, including the use of paper records. Rail passengers were unable to access e-tickets for their journeys as they couldn't open the emails in their Outlook inboxes. National Rail warned travellers to use alternative methods to access their tickets. A spokesman said: "We’re aware of the ongoing Microsoft global outage, which may be affecting customers’ ability to access their train tickets via their email inbox. "If you’re unable to locate or access your tickets through your email due to this issue, you may still be able to access your tickets by visiting the website or app where you purchased your tickets from and logging into your account. ‼️We’re aware of the ongoing Microsoft global outage, which may be affecting customers’ ability to access their train tickets via their email inbox. 🔗Latest Information and advice can be found here: https://t.co/pYa714hR8k — National Rail (@nationalrailenq) November 13, 2026 "We recommend doing this before you travel to ensure you have your tickets readily available for your journey. "This may not be possible if you checked out as a guest – please contact your ticket retailer directly if you are unable to access your tickets. "If you are still unable to access your ticket, please contact a member of onboard staff or station staff for advice." Other rail operators, including Southeastern, Chiltern Railways and London North Eastern Railway (LNER), reported similar problems with emailed tickets. Did the global Microsoft 365 outage affect you this week? Let us know in the comments below.

metadata.title: Rare fish 'considered locally extinct' found in Cambridgeshire
metadata.contentSnippet: A critically endangered species of fish has been discovered in a Cambridgeshire waterway, despite being thought to be extinct locally.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Rare fish 'considered locally extinct' found in Cambridgeshire
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: A rare fish thought to be extinct locally has been discovered in Cambridgeshire. The sturgeon, weighing 15lb, was found on the banks of the Twenty Foot Drain last week, the Environment Agency said. According to the Zoological Society of London, the UK is home to two native species of the fish. The Atlantic and European sturgeon can both reach up to five metres long and can live for more than 60 years. They are among the most critically endangered group of animals on the International Union for Conservation of Nature's Red List. The Environment Agency said it hadn't been made aware of any catch reports in the drains or surrounding rivers. "We have absolutely no idea what the story with this one is," a spokesperson said. They added: "Native sturgeon are considered locally extinct in our patch, although historically there have been reports from the River Great Ouse. "Reports exist of a 130lb sturgeon being caught in Huntingdon way back in 1754. "There have been introductions of the species in France in recent years with some of these fish migrating across the channel and being caught in UK waters." It is illegal to keep sturgeon in fisheries in England due to the risk of hybridisation with the few remaining native European sturgeon in the UK's waterways. Have you got a story you want to share? metadata.contentSnippet: The Ocean Film Festival World Tour is set to make waves at the West Road Concert Hall in Cambridge.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Ocean Film Festival World Tour to arrive in Cambridge
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: A cinematic celebration of the sea is set to make waves at the West Road Concert Hall in Cambridge. The Ocean Film Festival World Tour will arrive on November 26, with a new selection of ocean-themed short films capturing adventures above and below the waves. Now in its 13th year, the tour aims to inspire audiences with stories from the sea and those who dedicate their lives to protecting it. Nell Teasdale, UK tour director, said: "As we head into our 13th year, the Ocean Film Festival World Tour remains a celebration of the ocean in all its beauty, power and vulnerability. "Each film in the 2026 programme will offer something special, whether it’s extraordinary adventure, breath-taking marine life or people dedicating their lives to protecting the sea. "It’s always incredible to see audiences come out year after year – not just to watch beautiful films, but to feel part of something bigger." A standout film in this year’s line-up is The Raftsmen, which tells the story of a record-breaking Pacific Ocean crossing.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: A man from Huntingdonshire has indicated guilty pleas to a string of offences including making and distributing indecent images of children. Raymond Setchell, of Green Leys, St Ives, appeared at Peterborough Magistrates' Court for his first hearing at 10am on Friday (November 13). He is accused of making a total of 849 indecent images of children across categories A, B and C in January this year. It is alleged Setchell made 404 category A images, which are the most serious kind, of children, followed by 262 category B images and 183 category C images. Setchell is also accused of distributing indecent photographs over text message between October 2025 and January 2026. He is alleged to have possessed 13 extreme pornographic images and a prohibited image of a child. The 57-year-old indicated guilty pleas to all eight offences and was remanded on conditional bail for a sentencing hearing at Cambridge Crown Court. He is also required to register with the police in accordance with the Sexual Offences Act 2003. Have you got a story you want to share? metadata.title: UK food supplier used by Aldi collapses and closes with 662 jobs lost
metadata.contentSnippet: Kanes Foods - which supplied Aldi, Lidl, and Asda with salads, stir-fries, and sauces - has ceased trading after entering administration, with 662 jobs lost.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: UK food supplier used by Aldi collapses and closes with 662 jobs lost
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: A major UK food supplier has collapsed into administration and ceased trading, resulting in the loss of more than 650 jobs. Kanes Foods, established in 1989, produced pre-packaged salads, stir-fry products and sauces (with a short shelf life) for major supermarkets, including: After 37 years in business, Kanes Foods has collapsed into administration. Timothy Andrew Higgins, Edward Williams and Helen Wheeler-Jones of PwC were appointed joint administrators on Monday (November 9). Following the appointment, Kanes Foods ceased "with immediate effect", and all 662 employees were made redundant. Joint administrator and director at PwC, Tim Higgins, said: "It is deeply regrettable that a long-established business with a strong reputation has been left with no option but to enter administration, and that so many hard-working employees have lost their jobs as a result. "We recognise how difficult a time this is for employees and their families and we will support those affected through the redundancy process." Kanes Foods had been under financial and operational strain for several years. In June 2025, a failure at its wastewater treatment plant led to approximately £2 million in one-off costs and higher ongoing operating expenses. Further disruption came in August 2026, when drought-related supply issues affected trading during the crucial summer season. The company also faced continued losses, negative cash flow and uncertainty over future demand. Directors explored options such as refinancing and securing new investment, but no viable solutions were found. A fast-track sale process began in mid-September 2026, but administrators were unable to secure a going concern sale in time. Administrators said they will support affected employees in making claims to the Redundancy Payments Service. It has been a tough year for the UK high street, with several retailers entering administration or liquidation and others announcing widespread store closures. Major high street brands Claire's and Quiz have been forced to close all their remaining stores after falling into administration. UK fashion retailer Leading Labels is also set to close its remaining 15 stores after falling into liquidation in May. Whitbread closed all its standalone branded restaurants across the UK last month, affecting five brands: However, Queensway Inns and Common Table Group have now taken over 110 of these former Whitbread sites, saving them from closure. Poundland has filed a notice to appoint administrators, putting the future of its 150 stores and 11,000 employees at risk. metadata.title: Government confirms new State Pension rates – see how much pensioners will get
metadata.contentSnippet: Government confirms new State Pension rates – see how much pensioners will get, with the full new State Pension rising to £250.70 a week

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Government confirms new State Pension rates – see how much pensioners will get
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: Pensioners are set to receive a higher weekly State Pension from April 2027 after the Government announced the new payment rates for the next financial year. The full new State Pension will increase to £250.70 a week, up from £241.30, while the full basic State Pension will rise to £192.10 a week from £184.90. The increases amount to an extra £9.40 and £7.20 a week respectively, giving eligible pensioners hundreds of pounds more over the course of a year. The new figures have been set out in a House of Commons Library briefing published on Wednesday, November 11, covering the benefit and pension rates announced for the 2027/28 financial year. Both the basic and new State Pension will rise by 3.9% from April 2027, in line with the annual increase in average weekly earnings between May and July 2026. The increase is part of the Government's commitment to the State Pension triple lock, which means payments rise each year by the highest of inflation, average earnings growth or 2.5%. The full weekly rates will be: Over a full year, the increase works out at around £488.80 for someone receiving the full new State Pension and £374.40 for someone receiving the full basic State Pension. The new State Pension applies to people who reached State Pension age on or after April 6, 2016. The basic State Pension is the core payment under the old State Pension system, for people who reached State Pension age before that date. The figures are the full weekly rates. The amount an individual receives will depend on their National Insurance record and whether they qualify for the full entitlement. Recommended reading: Pension Credit is also set to rise by 3.9% from April 2027, with the standard minimum guarantee increasing to: Pension Credit is a means-tested benefit designed to top up the income of people who have reached State Pension age and are on a lower income. It can also provide access to other support, including help with housing costs and some health-related expenses.

metadata.title: Millions could be affected by DWP benefits decision – full limits revealed
metadata.contentSnippet: The DWP plans to freeze the Benefit Cap for 2027/28. See the proposed weekly, monthly and annual limits for couples and single households.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Millions could be affected by DWP benefits decision – full limits revealed
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: The DWP has revealed they plan to freeze the maximum amount Brits can claim in benefits from next year. The Department for Work and Pensions updated their website on Wednesday, November 11, to outline proposed benefits rates for the 2027-28 tax year. Benefits caps are used by the government to limit the total amount of money claimants can receive and it applies to most people over 16 and below State Pensions age. -Widowed Parent’s Allowance (or Widowed Mother’s Allowance or Widow’s Pension if you started getting it before 9 April 2001) The current annual maximum for couples (with or without children) or single claimants with a child of qualifying age is £22,020 or £25,323 for those in Greater London. The annual maximum for single adults households this tax year, which ends in April, is £14,753 or £16,967 in Greater London. This is proposed to be frozen for the 2027-28 tax year, meaning Brits won't be able to claim more than this amount between April 2027 and 2028. The monthly equivalent is also planned to be frozen at £1,835 and £2,110.25 (Greater London) for couples, with or without children, or single claimants with a child of qualifying age. Single households without children face the same freeze, with the maximum remaining at £1,229.42 and £1,413.92 in Greater London. Weekly equivalents are planned to remain at £423.46 and £486.98 (Greater London) for couples, with or without children, or single claimants with a qualifying-age. The weekly maximum for single households is planned to remain at £283.71 or £326.29 (Greater London). This is despite the Office for National Statistics' most recent inflation rate being recorded at 3.6% in September and many economists forecasting that this is expected to rise next year. The government explains that the cap may not start for nine months if someone is claiming Universal Credit but this depends on their earnings. Recommended reading: Brits are not affected by the benefits cap if they or their partner get Universal Credit because of a disability that 'stops them from working' or get it because they care for someone with a disability. They're also exempt if they get Universal Credit and they or their partner earn £881 or more a month combined, after tax and National Insurance contributions.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: Two pie products sold at Tesco have been recalled due to the packaging being labelled incorrectly. The affected items are the Tesco Steak and Guinness Pie (200g) and the Tesco 6 Steak and Guinness Mini Pies (198g). These items contain milk but their packaging does not declare it, posing a possible risk to anyone who is allergic to milk or has an intolerance to milk or milk constituents. All use-by dates of both products up to and including November 23, 2026 are being recalled. Recommended reading: “Sometimes foods have to be withdrawn or recalled if there is a risk to consumers because the allergy labelling is missing or incorrect or if there is any other food allergy risk. “When there is a food allergy risk, the FSA will issue an Allergy Alert.” Do you shop at Tesco? metadata.title: UK airline ordered into compulsory liquidation 7 years after being founded
metadata.contentSnippet: The virtual UK airline Global Airlines has been ordered into compulsory liquidation seven years after it was founded in 2019

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: UK airline ordered into compulsory liquidation 7 years after being founded
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: Global Airlines has been ordered into compulsory liquidation following a winding-up petition. The UK startup, which planned to use a fleet of Airbus A380 planes, was formally ordered to wind up by the Insolvency and Companies Court on Wednesday, November 4. The winding-up petition was originally filed in May, with several hearings held in the following months, including the most recent in October. The Gazette published the notice on Thursday, November 12, confirming the order. Former company directors Tom Stokely and Prashant Uttamchandani joined the case as supporting creditors and were represented by the law firm Katten Muchin Rosenman. With the order now in place, an officer of the court—known as the official receiver—has taken control of winding up the company. Government guidelines state that once a winding-up order is issued, the company’s bank accounts are typically frozen and its assets sold off to repay creditors. Companies have the right to apply for cancellation of a winding-up order within five working days if they believe the action is unwarranted. As of the latest update, Global Airlines is still listed as active on Companies House, though its most recent accounts are overdue. Global Airlines has been contacted by Newsquest for comment. Global Airlines Limited operated as a virtual airline with ambitions to operate a fleet of four Airbus A380 aircraft. The company, which was founded in 2019, acquired its only aircraft in May 2023, and claimed to be the first new A380 owner in eight years. Its maiden flight, operated under a damp lease from Hi Fly Malta, flew from Glasgow to New York-JFK on May 15, 2025. After completing just four transatlantic flights, the aircraft was placed into long-term storage in Tarbes, France, on July 16, 2025, with no known return-to-service date. Discussing its vision for the company, Global Airlines shared: "We want to deliver the Best Way to Fly. "And whether flying Global Traveller, Business or First, we believe we will. "Flying to a variety of destinations all over the world, we will breathe new life into onboard product and service, working with some amazing brands, delivering genuine value for money for our passengers. "And by embracing the latest technology and deploying it across every touch point, we can work smarter and deliver a Global experience that is unique to you." metadata.contentSnippet: The DWP has confirmed new Universal Credit rates from April 2027, with payments rising for people who need care or help with mobility

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: DWP disability benefit increase from 2027 for people who need care or mobility help
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: The DWP revealed that a million Brits could receive more Disability Living Allowance money from April next year. The Department for Work and Pensions updated their website on November 11 with proposals to increase the weekly payments. The current rates only cover the tax year between April 6 2026 and April 5 2027 so from April 6 next year new rates will apply. These increases are labelled as 'provisional' but the Government website's update history shows the previous provisional figures reflected the final figures to the penny. Disability Living Allowance, which helps cover the costs of extra personal care or mobility, has two components - care and mobility. Both of these are split from highest to lowest rates of payment depending on how severe the need for support is. People are eligible for the care component if they need help with things like washing, eating, cooking, communicating needs, dressing or using the toilet. They may also need supervision to 'avoid putting yourself or others in danger' or to have dialysis. The highest rate is paid to those who need 'help or supervision throughout both day and night, or if a medical professional has said they're nearing the end of their life'. This payment is proposed to rise from the £114.60 per week being paid during the current tax year to £118.60 per week for the 2027-28 tax year. The middle rate is described as being suitable for those who need 'frequent help or constant supervision during the day, supervision at night or someone to help you while on dialysis'. The lowest rate is for those who 'need help for some of the day or with preparing cooked meals' and this rate is proposed to increase from £30.30 per week to £31.35. The mobility component is for people who either cannot walk, can only walk 'short distances without severe discomfort' or who could become 'very ill if they try to walk'. People may also get this if they have no feet or legs, are 100% blind or you were between ages 3-64 on April 11 2011 and have been certified as 'severely sight impaired'. Recommended reading: Other criteria include those at least 80% deaf, those who need someone with them when outdoors or those who are 'severely mentally impaired' with behavioural problems. The lower rate of payment is for those who need 'guidance or supervision outdoors' and this would rise from £30.30 per week to £31.35 in the 2027-28 tax year. The higher rate is for those who have 'any other, more severe, walking difficulty' than covered in the lower rate and this would increase from £80 to £82.80 under the proposed new rates. Payments are usually sent directly to claimants bank accounts every four weeks and if their circumstances change they are told to contact the Disability Service Centre.

metadata.title: MoneySavingExpert warns Virgin customers to check for 'sneaky' paid add-on
metadata.contentSnippet: MoneySavingExpert says Virgin Experience Days shoppers should check for a £9.99 annual membership they may not have intended to buy.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: MoneySavingExpert warns Virgin customers to check for 'sneaky' paid add-on
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: Virgin Experience Days shoppers are being urged to check whether they were signed up to a paid membership without realising. MoneySavingExpert said its team found the £9.99-a-year Memory Makers+ subscription was being added to orders through a pre-ticked box at checkout. The consumer website said it spotted the issue when it visited the company's website on October 30 and reported it to the Competition and Markets Authority (CMA). MoneySavingExpert said Virgin Experience Days changed its website after the issue was raised, so the membership box was no longer selected by default. The membership offers discounts on purchases, free greeting cards and other benefits, and renews automatically each year. CMA guidance says businesses must obtain a customer's express consent before charging for optional extras. It says a pre-ticked box does not provide that consent when a customer must take action to avoid an extra charge. The regulator also says customers who did not expressly agree to an additional charge are legally entitled to claim a refund. MoneySavingExpert recommends searching email inboxes, including junk and spam folders, for an account activation message to check whether the membership was added. It advises customers who want to cancel or request a refund to contact memorymakers@virginexperiencedays.co.uk. A Virgin Experience Days spokesperson said: "Memory Makers+ remains a relatively new addition to our business, and we continually review and refine the programme based on performance data, customer feedback and regulatory developments." The company said most customers saved more than the cost of membership on their first purchase and that it received positive feedback about the scheme. The spokesperson added: "In the small number of cases where a customer wishes to cancel, we operate a seven day a week support operation where queries are handled within 24 hours."

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: Microsoft users are still reporting issues with several of its services including Outlook. People have taken to Downdetector to report the issues with over 3,000 reports being made at around 6pm last night (Thursday, November 12). The number of reports of Microsoft Outlook being down is currently rising again with 1,115 reports being made at 6am this morning (Friday, November 13). 29% of people have reported issues with logging in to Outlook while 26% have said they are struggling to receive messages and 23% are having issues with the app. We're investigating reports of users experiencing issues accessing Exchange Online mailboxes through multiple connection methods in the Americas. More details can be found in the Microsoft 365 admin center under EX1550543. — Microsoft 365 Status (@MSFT365Status) November 12, 2026 Microsoft released a statement yesterday sharing that the issues with its apps started in the US but has spread to areas across the world. Microsoft said: “We're investigating reports of users experiencing issues accessing Exchange Online mailboxes through multiple connection methods in the Americas. More details can be found in the Microsoft 365 admin center under EX1550543. “While we’re working to mitigate impact, we’ve confirmed the issue may affect Microsoft 365 service connectivity for users in any region, more information will be provided in the Microsoft 365 admin center under EX1550543. “We’ve determined a portion of infrastructure is experiencing elevated load across multiple regions, which is likely contributing to the connectivity errors. “We're providing more information under EX1550543 and MO1550821 in the Microsoft 365 admin center, as well as https://status.cloud.microsoft.” As well as Outlook, Microsoft users are facing issues with several other apps including Microsoft 365 with over 600 people reporting issues this morning. Over 100 people have taken to Downdetector and have reported issues with Teams. Others have reported issues with Copilot and the Microsoft store. Microsoft has confirmed the fixes are not going "as expected" with the team still trying to find new ways to restore its services. It has tried several solutions to the problem such as isolating parts of its infrastructure and shifting traffic to alternate routes. Charles Lamanna, Microsoft's executive vice-president, has said the outages do not appear to be because of a cyber attack. Microsoft said: “We’ve monitored the status of the changes applied to improve serviceability and confirmed that change is not taking as expected." Downdetector is a website that allows users of popular services like Instagram, Facebook, and Virgin Media to share if they are having trouble with the services. Describing itself on its website, Downdetector is “where people go when services don’t work.” The site will also collect information about any service problems from social media and other factors on the web. An incident is detected if the number of reports is significantly higher than the typical average for that service. Have you been struggling to access Microsoft services? metadata.title: M&S apologises after customer ate 'crispy moth' lurking in tortilla chips
metadata.contentSnippet: Suzanne Bailey says she found a moth in M&S tortilla crisps served with a family meal. M&S apologised and said it was investigating.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: M&S apologises after customer ate 'crispy moth' lurking in tortilla chips
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: A woman says she found a moth in her M&S tortilla crisps after eating a third of the bag. Suzanne Bailey said she initially thought the object was a burnt tortilla when she served the crisps with a family meal. The 45-year-old said she then realised it was a moth, which she believed had been cooked with the crisps. M&S apologised, offered her a refund and said it was investigating with its supplier. The operations manager, from Liverpool, had bought a £1.25 bag of lightly salted tortilla crisps for a Mexican meal. She said her 13-year-old daughter Isabella had eaten one crisp and was sick after the discovery. Ms Bailey said: "I went to pick the burnt tortilla up and this is when I realised it was a moth. My little girl had a mouthful of food and threw up. "I was mortified as I had eaten approximately a third of the bag." She said she found what she believed were the moth's legs when she returned the crisps to the bag as evidence, leaving her concerned she might have eaten one. Ms Bailey added: "It's gross and absolutely disgusting. I'm not into bushtucker trials but it feels like I've done an M&S one. "We haven't been back to shop at M&S. I don't think I could eat tortilla chips again either." After the incident, she threw away the £10 meal and ordered a £20 takeaway to feed her family instead. After taking photographs, she said she submitted a complaint through the M&S website and called customer support. An M&S spokesperson said: "We take matters like this extremely seriously and are working closely with our supplier partner to investigate this fully." The spokesperson said: "We have been in touch with the customer directly to apologise for the inconvenience caused and offer a full refund."

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Royal Mint Beatrix Potter 50p coin sells for more than 400 times face value on eBay
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: A Royal Mint Peter Rabbit 50p coin has sold on eBay for more than £200. The Royal Mint's Beatrix Potter collection began in 2016, marking 150 years since the author's birth. The first Peter Rabbit design showed a close-up of the character facing forward, complete with whiskers. Other 2016 designs featured Squirrel Nutkin, Mrs Tiggy-Winkle and Jemima Puddle-Duck. Four more designs arrived in 2017, featuring Tom Kitten, Benjamin Bunny, Jeremy Fisher and another Peter Rabbit. The 2018 Peter Rabbit and Flopsy Bunny designs each had a circulating mintage of 1.4 million. The Peter Rabbit editions from 2019 and 2020 were not put into general circulation. The seller described the coin as a 2016 Royal Mint Peter Rabbit 50p in silver proof, with a fineness of 0.925. The listing eventually sold for a total of £219.20, including a £9.03 buyer-protection fee. The Royal Mint lists the 2023 Atlantic Salmon 50p as the rarest circulating 50p, with a mintage of 200,000. Next on its list is the 2009 Kew Gardens 50p, with 210,000, followed by the 2011 Olympic football design, with 1,125,500. The date matters: the Royal Mint's table also records two million Atlantic Salmon 50p coins dated 2025. Other low-mintage circulating designs include the 2011 Olympic wrestling, judo and triathlon coins, alongside the 2018 Peter Rabbit and Flopsy Bunny 50ps. Mintage is the number of coins made, and a lower figure can make a design harder for collectors to find. A coin's condition, design, material and demand from collectors can also affect what someone is willing to pay. A genuine error can be of interest to collectors, but a seller's description alone is not independent verification. The Royal Mint advises buyers of second-hand coins to check for original packaging and, for proof editions, a certificate of authenticity. A specialist valuation can help an owner establish a coin's history and likely value.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: Millions of leaseholders are set to gain new powers to challenge unfair service charges. The government says more than three million leaseholders in England will benefit from the reforms, with the first changes planned for April 1, 2027. The measures are due to be introduced in stages through to November 2028, subject to parliamentary approval. From April 2027, leaseholders will be able to request information about their service charges, including details from previous years. Landlords will need a good reason to refuse to provide the information, according to the Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government. Service charges are fees paid by leaseholders or tenants to cover the maintenance, repair and management of shared areas of a building. The ministry says the changes will give leaseholders a clearer picture of how their building is managed, maintained, repaired and insured. The first stage also includes stronger protection against having to pay a landlord's legal costs when challenging a charge. Landlords will need court or tribunal approval to pass on legal costs, while leaseholders will gain a right to recover their own legal expenses, the government says. Further measures are planned for November 1, 2027, when leaseholders will receive clearer information about charges, including details of building insurance and administration fees. There will also be stronger protections against excessive or unreasonable fees for arranging and managing insurance. Private landlords will have to use standardised service charge demand forms and provide financial accounts and annual reports from November 2027. Councils and housing associations will have until November 1, 2028 to introduce those forms, accounts and reports for their leaseholders. Kion Ahadi, chief executive of the Leasehold Advisory Service, said: "Service charges are the most common issue leaseholders contact us about. "We welcome these changes as an important step forward in helping people understand what they are paying for and challenge costs they believe are unfair. "Leaseholders need clear information about how their money is being spent and a fair opportunity to raise concerns. "Better access to that information and stronger protection from landlords’ legal bills will give them more confidence to hold their landlord to account."

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: Millions of people claiming Universal Credit are set to receive a higher monthly payment next year, after the Department for Work and Pensions (DWP) confirmed the new benefit rates. The Government has published its annual review of benefit payments, setting out how much claimants will receive from April 2027. Working-age and disability benefits will rise by 3.5%, with the new rates mainly coming into effect from April 12, 2027. Inflation-linked benefits and tax credits will rise by 3.5% from April 2027, in line with the annual increase in the Consumer Prices Index (CPI) rate of inflation for September 2026. Universal Credit standard allowances will receive an additional uplift as specified in the Universal Credit Act 2025. The basic and new State Pensions will be uprated by 3.9% from April 2027, in line with the annual increase in the Average Weekly Earnings (AWE) index for May–July 2026. Universal Credit is currently paid to more than 8.4 million people across the UK. Due to the increase in line with CPI, and the additional uprating factor, in 2027/28 Universal Credit standard allowances will increase: Universal Credit is a means-tested benefit designed to help with living costs for people on a low income, out of work or unable to work. The number of people claiming it has increased as the DWP continues its managed migration programme, which is moving people from older benefits onto the newer system. Around 2.2 million Universal Credit claimants are in employment, while a significant number of others are not expected to work because of health conditions or caring responsibilities. Recommended reading: Work and Pensions Secretary Pat McFadden confirmed the increases in a statement to Parliament following the Budget. He said: “The new rates will apply in the tax year 2027-28 and will mainly come into effect from April 12 2027. “The other state pension and benefit rates covered by my statutory review will be increased by 3.5%, in line with the increase in the consumer prices index in the year to September 2026. “This includes most working-age benefits and other benefits for people below state pension age; benefits to help with additional needs arising from disability; statutory payments including statutory sick pay and statutory maternity pay; and additional state pension. The pension credit savings credit maximum amount will also increase by 3.5%.”

metadata.title: Met Police opens investigation into David Walliams after sexual offences allegations

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: The Metropolitan Police has launched an investigation after the force received “a number of allegations of non-recent serious sexual offences” against David Walliams. It comes after Walliams was named as the celebrity who tried to block the publication of his identity amid allegations of “inappropriate sexual activities” with girls and young women earlier this week. Multiple women have accused the comedian, 55, of sexually inappropriate behaviour and grooming, including when they were teenagers, according to an investigation by the Guardian and ITV News. Walliams denies all allegations against him. David Walliams has denied all allegatons made against him (Image: Aaron Chown/PA) The Met Police received a number of non-recent allegations against the former Britain’s Got Talent judge “in recent days”. In a statement on Friday (November 13), the Met said the complaints made are separate from those previously reported by ITV News and The Guardian. But it added those reports are being reviewed by officers “to establish whether there is any evidence of offences”. A joint investigation by ITV News and The Guardian alleges Walliams preyed on teenage girls and young women for sexual purposes. Multiple women accuse Walliams of “grooming” them as teenagers, while another described her alleged encounter with Walliams as “sexual assault”. Walliams is also accused of inappropriate conduct and sexual harassment at his former publisher HarperCollins, and while working on Britain’s Got Talent. 🚨 BREAKING: David Walliams is now being investigated by the Met Police over alleged "serious sexual offences" https://t.co/udBrHX7noC — Politics UK (@PolitlcsUK) November 13, 2026 Responding to the ITV and Guardian investigation, Walliams denied all allegations against him. He said: "Looking back, I realise that at times I behaved thoughtlessly towards other people I had casual sexual relationships with... I realise I did not always take people’s feelings properly into account. That is something I regret. “And whilst a power imbalance is inevitable when one party is famous, abusing that power is something else entirely and it is something that I never did... “I am not a sexual predator... I have not broken the law... I am devastated that some of the women I met ten to twenty years ago have now expressed hurt or anger towards me.” The former Britain’s Got Talent judge, known for appearing in comedy shows including Come Fly With Me and Little Britain alongside Matt Lucas, has sold more than 60 million copies of his children’s books globally. They include The Boy In The Dress, Fing, and Gangsta Granny, the latter of which was turned into a one-hour BBC special in 2013, followed by a sequel starring Sheridan Smith in 2022. Walliams’ book publisher HarperCollins dropped him in December 2025, after an investigation into allegations he had “harassed” young women, which Walliams strongly denied. Earlier this month, theme park Alton Towers permanently closed its World of David Walliams attraction, which featured rides inspired by the books. Walliams left Britain’s Got Talent in 2022 after he apologised for making “disrespectful comments” about auditioning contestants during filming breaks in January 2020 at the London Palladium. In 2023, Britain’s Got Talent producer Fremantle apologised and reached an “amicable resolution” with Walliams after the remarks he made while on the show were leaked.

metadata.title: Watch moment ATM thief found hiding in loft after nationwide crime spree
metadata.contentSnippet: A prolific thief who targeted cash machines across England and Wales, including Cambridgeshire, has been jailed.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Watch moment ATM thief found hiding in loft after nationwide crime spree
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: A prolific thief who targeted cash machines across England and Wales, including Cambridgeshire, has been jailed. Bogdan Gasparov, 40, used cash-trapping devices to steal more than £16,000 from at least 180 ATMs between May and October 2026. Police found him hiding in a loft crawl space during a raid on his Hardie Road home in Dagenham. Detective Sergeant Mike Simpson from ERSOU's Proactive Economic Crime Team (PECT) said: "This was not opportunistic offending. "Gasparov carried out a calculated campaign of theft, targeting cash machines across the country and repeatedly returning to steal money that belonged to unsuspecting customers. "What makes this case even more brazen is that Gasparov had previously been convicted for similar offences and deported from the UK, only to return illegally and resume the same criminal behaviour. "He clearly believed he could stay one step ahead of investigators. He couldn't. "Thanks to the determination of our officers and the strength of the evidence gathered, he has now been brought to justice once again." Gasparov targeted ATMs in Bury St Edmunds, Lowestoft and Sudbury in Suffolk, Great Yarmouth in Norfolk, Huntingdon and Peterborough in Cambridgeshire, and Harlow in Essex. He also struck near Nottingham, Oxford, Somerset, Bristol, Derby, Gloucester, Lincoln and the West Midlands, as well as in parts of Scotland and Wales. The scheme involved Gasparov posing as a legitimate customer, fitting homemade cash-trapping devices to ATMs, and leaving the area. When genuine customers attempted to withdraw money, the cash would become trapped in the device. Gasparov would then return later to retrieve the device and the stolen funds. CCTV from several locations repeatedly placed Gasparov at the scenes. A search of his vehicle uncovered clothing worn during the offences, homemade cash-trapping devices and tools to make them. Moldovan national Gasparov used several aliases and had previous convictions for similar crimes. He had re-entered the UK illegally after being deported. Within 24 hours of his arrest, he pleaded guilty at Chelmsford Magistrates’ Court to two counts of theft from an ATM, covering all the offences. He also admitted entering the UK in breach of a deportation order and possessing items for use in fraud. On November 9, Gasparov was jailed for three years and six months at Chelmsford Crown Court. He is expected to face another deportation hearing after his release.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: Extra support has been made available to victims of crime in Cambridgeshire and Peterborough. The support is in response to concerns arising from the Early Release Scheme, which is seeing some offenders released from prison before their full sentence is served. Police and Crime Commissioner Darryl Preston has increased the capacity of the Victim and Witness Hub to ensure timely and comprehensive support for those affected. Darryl said: "I understand the anxiety such news could cause especially for victims of domestic violence. "That's why I am keen to raise awareness of the local offer of support available here in our county to ensure victims feel safe, informed and supported." The Victim and Witness Hub offers emotional and practical support, including referrals to home security services and enhanced emotional support programmes. Victim and Witness Care Co-ordinators can also reconnect individuals with specialist services they have previously used. Victims whose offenders are being released early will be notified and directed to support services in their area. For those worried about personal safety, the Bobby Scheme is available to provide home security assessments and install devices such as locks and video doorbells. Additional funding of £195,000 over two years has been allocated to increase support services. A national Offender Release Helpline, set up by Victim Support, is also available on 0808 168 9280. The helpline operates Monday to Friday from 9am to 5pm, excluding bank holidays. The Early Release Scheme, known as the Progression Model, applies to offenders with fixed-term sentences. It allows part of the sentence to be served in the community under supervision. All individuals released under the scheme are subject to licence conditions and a period of intensive supervision. Victims in Cambridgeshire seeking support can contact the Victim and Witness Hub on 0800 781 6818 or by emailing victimandwitnesshub@cambs.police.uk.

metadata.title: Support for pubs only ‘lip service’ after budget says landlady
metadata.contentSnippet: A Cambridge pub landlady has accused the government of only paying “lip service” to supporting hospitality following the latest budget.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Support for pubs only ‘lip service’ after budget says landlady
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: A Cambridge pub landlady has accused the government of only paying “lip service” to supporting hospitality following the latest budget. Chancellor of the Exchequer John Healey delivered the first budget of Andy Burnham’s government last month, with a number of changes for pubs. This includes raising the threshold for Small Business Rates Relief in England from £12k to £18k – meaning businesses with a rateable value below this will pay no business rates. But pub operators will also face higher wage bills with the national living wage for workers aged 21 and over increasing from £12.71 an hour to £13.21. Both changes will come into effect from April 2027 and alcohol duty will also increase in line with inflation from February 1. Hayley Pellegrini, who runs five pubs in the city with her husband Steve including The Portland Arms and The Alex, said she does not feel small businesses are getting the support they need. The 56-year-old said: “We work ridiculous hours and what we pay ourselves we worked out is probably below minimum wage. “But it’s a case of we just have to suck it up and get on with it. “I don’t feel like we are getting the support we need – they aren’t doing anything, they want to be seen as being pub goers and that but they aren’t doing anything. “It’s not just pubs, it’s small businesses in general – we have friends who have small businesses and they are struggling as well.” She said small businesses are discouraged from expanding as they will lose relief and face higher wage bills from increased national insurance contributions and the rise in wages. Ms Pellegrini said it was harder for them as a living-wage employer, but that they’re “fortunate” to be based in Cambridge with a steady stream of business from students and tourists. She said: “Why am I going to employ someone with no experience, when I could be paying someone with ten years of experience the same? I think we are losing the next generation of hospitality managers, in 10 or 15 years we might find we haven’t brought up the next generation of managers.” She said the government was being “narrowminded” by not considering a reduction in VAT – with more than 400,000 signing the VAT’s the Problem petition to cut it from 20 per cent to 10 per cent, in line with other countries in Europe like France, Spain and Italy. Ms Pellegrini said: “We were hoping that Andy Burnham was actually going to be the one who will do something, but now we think – ‘ah, here we go again’. “What worries me is our retirement – we’re so busy trying to keep the business afloat we aren’t actually able to put anything away for our retirement and we’re going to be a burden on the government. “I work long, unsociable, hours often seven days a week to keep this industry going – who am I doing this for? “The slice of the pie being taken off us is just getting bigger and bigger and bigger. “It seems to be targeted at small businesses while companies like Amazon pay a tiny proportion of tax. “Something needs to be redistributed – the rich are getting richer and the rest of us are working our butts off to try and make a living.”

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: A council wants permission to fly three flags outside its main offices. Huntingdonshire District Council is seeking permission from its own planning officers to fly the Emergency Services, Remembrance Day and LGBTQ+ Progress Pride flags each year at Pathfinder House in St Mary’s Street, Huntingdon. Caroline Wilson, who submitted the application on behalf of the council, said: "We have been flying all flags annually before realising we needed consent." Reform UK councillors criticised the council for flying the Progress Pride Flag during Pride Month in June. Reform UK members argued the flag was "divisive" and lacked the necessary planning consent. Cllr Ryan Coogan, Reform group leader, said at the time that councils should not fly "divisive political symbols", particularly where the correct permissions have not been obtained, and stressed that public buildings should represent everyone in the district. The council later admitted it lacked permission to fly the flag, but said it only realised this as the flag was being taken down. A spokesperson for the council said: "The Pride Progress flag is a variant of the original Gilbert Baker Pride flag, adopted widely by members of the LGBTQ+ community and related groups. "In planning terms, the Pride flag benefits from 'deemed consent' under the Town and Country Planning (Control of Advertisements) Regulations 2007 (as amended). "However, the Pride Progress flag is not covered by this provision and therefore requires express consent from the local planning authority." The Progress Pride Flag updates the traditional rainbow design to represent more communities within the LGBTQ+ movement. The council said the flag was taken down to make way for the Armed Forces Day Flag, which was flown in honour of Armed Forces Day on June 27. Reform UK councillors said they raised concerns after being contacted by residents about the flag being displayed on a public building. They said this prompted them to challenge its display. Huntingdonshire District Council first raised a Progress Pride flag at Pathfinder House in June 2022, saying it symbolised representation of everyone in the district.

A hospital redevelopment is moving forward with a fresh environmental impact assessment underway. Plans to rebuild Hinchingbrooke Hospital have reached a new stage after North West Anglia NHS Foundation Trust submitted a revised Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA) Scoping Report to Huntingdonshire District Council (HDC). The report sets out key changes and asks the council for a new EIA Scoping Opinion to inform the Environmental Statement for the planned application. The trust previously secured an EIA Scoping Opinion from HDC in October 2025, based on proposals developed in August 2025. An artist's impression of what the new staff accommodation will look like and what the courtyard area will look like once installed by Zed Pods Ltd. (Image: North West Anglia NHS Foundation Trust) Since then, the scheme has undergone further design changes, prompting the need for a revised EIA. The updated plans include a range of modifications to the original development. These include the removal of the lower ground floor from the new hospital building, the addition of an energy centre north of the main building, and the relocation of the ambulance deck to the south-east of the site. Land at Views Common could be used temporarily as a contractor’s compound during construction, which may last up to eight years, subject to a lease agreement with the owner. The northern car park will remain at ground level, with possible solar canopies added. Plans for a multi-storey car park have been scrapped. A separate application is being prepared for car parking on the adjacent Constabulary Land, which has been removed from the main hospital application. The trust plans to submit an outline application covering new hospital buildings, an energy centre, service and administration facilities, parking, cycle storage, landscaping, drainage and improved access from Views Common Road. It will also cover the phased demolition of existing hospital buildings and the removal of some trees protected by Tree Preservation Orders. Approved enabling works include relocating staff accommodation, demolishing former staff blocks and creating a temporary car park. The trust is seeking separate permission for the Constabulary Land car park to maintain parking capacity during construction. A separate application also covers a new main intake substation to provide the hospital with an independent high-voltage electricity supply. The latest EIA Scoping Report confirms that most environmental topics identified in the 2025 assessment remain relevant. However, archaeology has now been scoped in due to the discovery of ridge and furrow earthworks and the high potential for further archaeological remains at Views Common. It also explains how the project will assess air quality, biodiversity, noise and vibration, transport and access, trees, daylight and sunlight, and wind. The trust is working with HDC, statutory consultees and other stakeholders to keep the planning process on track with the project and policy requirements. The site boundary has been redrawn to reflect the latest design, removing areas covered by separate applications and adding land at Views Common. The report says the development is not vulnerable to major accidents or disasters, so those risks will not be assessed further. That conclusion is based on the site’s location, existing safeguards and lack of nearby hazards such as major pipelines. The report also includes an assessment of how climate change could affect the development and how it can withstand those risks. It considers sudden and long-term climate hazards, the vulnerability of key site elements and existing measures to adapt. The assessment will be developed further as the design progresses. The EIA Scoping Report will support the updated hospital planning application and shape its Environmental Statement. HDC is expected to issue a revised Scoping Opinion after consulting statutory bodies and reviewing the report. Hinchingbrooke is one of seven English hospitals being rebuilt through the national New Hospital Programme because of RAAC, with the new facility expected to open by the end of 2032.

metadata.title: Poundland issues major update as UK stores at risk of closure
metadata.contentSnippet: Poundland has issued an update today (November 12) as it continues to try to secure a potential rescue deal.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Poundland issues major update as UK stores at risk of closure
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: Poundland has issued an update today (November 12), following the end of a 10-day period that allowed it to continue to try and secure a potential rescue deal. In recent months, the future of Poundland has been uncertain, with last-ditch efforts hoping to save the struggling retailer. The chain filed a notice of intention to appoint administrators at the end of October, which expired at midnight last night. Asked if the company was going into administration on Thursday, managing director Barry Williams told reporters: “We’re going to go and have a board meeting now to have those conversations.” Now, Poundland has issued an update, informing customers of its future plans. Poundland customers have been assured that its stores are open as normal for at least the next 10 working days. The Board of Poundland Limited said: “Over the past two weeks, Poundland has been operating under the statutory protection of a Notice of Intention (NOI) to appoint Administrators. “Amid an ongoing sale process, and with funding agreed to enable the business to continue trading during this period, the Board of Poundland has today resolved to make an application for a second NOI with a view to identifying the best available prospects for shareholders, creditors and our people. “This extends the current protections over the business for a further 10 working days. “Our stores remain open as usual during this period, and we thank our colleagues, suppliers and customers for their incredible and continued support.” Poundland has roughly 600 shops and 11,000 employees across the UK. Ahead of the announcement, Reform UK deputy leader Richard Tice said: “Hopefully the directors will be able to extend the notice of administration period from tonight to allow time for a deal to be done with a new buyer for Poundland. “This will protect many thousands of jobs and keep an important value retailer on the High Street, for hard-pressed consumers worried about rising bills.” After a meeting with MPs on the Commons Business, Innovation, Science and Trade Committee, Mr Williams thanked the chain’s staff, whose jobs are at risk. He told Sky News he was “representing 11,000 colleagues” as well as thousands in the broader supply chain and “maybe even the retail industry” at the meeting. Asked whether he could guarantee the security of jobs and keep the business going in the run-up to Christmas, he said there were “no guarantees at this point”. It is understood that Poundland’s owners, Gordon Brothers, have enabled the release of around £10 million of funding for things such as paying staff, taxes and suppliers of stock. The extension to Wednesday’s deadline could mean the prospect of a deal that would satisfy the company’s creditors remains on the table. Advisers have been in talks with parties interested in buying the brand or parts of the business such as swathes of shops. Recommended reading: It has held talks with potential bidders including Tesco over proposals to buy up to 150 stores, and other chains such as Iceland and Lidl. Investment firm Xyra Holdings emerged as a potential buyer for the whole business, while Irish firm Martin Property Group is believed to remain interested. Gordon Brothers previously rejected a takeover offer from Martin Property Group but management named the firm as the preferred bidder last month. Would you like to see Poundland remain on UK high streets? Let us know in the comments below.
